FOREWORD 

This book is the result of the experience of the writer and the contributors hereto in the handling of real estate transactions. The authenticity of the information contained herein, is believed to be reliable and authoritative but is not intended as a legal guide or to supplant the services of practicing attorneysat-law. In the handling of legal matters where the services of competent legal counsel are indicated it is recommended that you consult your attorney.

It is designed for the use of real estate brokers and salesmen as a guide and reference book covering problems with which they are confronted in their daily practice of the real estate profession. 

It is also intended to be in such complete form covering State Real Estate requirements, that those desiring Real Estate Broker's or salesman's licenses will find here all necessary information compiled in a manner to be easily assimilated.

Section I General Information CHANGES IN THE LAWS OF CALIFORNIA Affecting Real Estate Brokers and Property Owners 

1. Notice of change in terms and of termination of month to month tenancies of real property may now be given on the first day of the rental term, effective a month later, whereas formerly, a full thirty days' notice excluding the first day of the term was necessary. 

2. A homestead of real property standing in the name of wife and husband as joint tenants, may be declared by the husband. whereas formerly the husband had no right to declare a homestead on joint tenancy property held by himself and wife. 

3. An agreement to assume an indebtedness secured by a mortgage or deed of trust must now either be in writing or contained in the deed to real property; formerly an oral agreement to assume such an indebtedness was good. 

4. Where property is sold to pay a court judgment, redemption from sale within a year may now be had upon paying eight per cent interest from date of sale instead of twelve per cent, as formerly. 

5. A judgment debtor may now file a notice in the Recorder's office and have notice by registered mail of any sale under execution; formerly notice by posting was sufficient. 

6. Future street improvement bonds under the 1911 and 1915 

Acts will bear 6% instead of the seven per cent now generally charged. 

7. Business opportunity brokers and salesmen must now be licensed as well as yacht and ship brokers. 

8. Landlord and tenant under written term lease, may now agree in writing that suit for damages for failure of tenant to complete his term may be brought immediately after tenant's default under lease; formerly such an action could not be brought until the expiration of the term. 

9. An expert witness may now testify in court as to his reasons for reaching certain conclusions; formerly a real estate appraiser, for example, could be asked his valuation of the property, but could not explain how he reached that figure except upon crossexamination. 

10. The Real Estate Brokers Law amended to permit revocation of license on any ground which would have been a ground for denying license had same been known prior to application. 

This is a new broad ground for revocation of brokers' licenses under procedure provided for in the Law. 

11. Trust Deeds that were executed subsequent to 1939, where foreclosure is made without court action, as authorized in the in- 

---

strument, no deficiency judgment is allowed. If foreclosed by court procedure, and the property sells for enough to pay the balance due and all charges, there is a three (3) month period of redemption allowed the owner. If, under court foreclosure, the property fails to sell for enough to cover the balance due, plus all charges, a deficiency judgment may be secured against the Trustor; in this case, however, the Trustor is granted one (1) year period of redemption. 

The above constitute substantially all of the amendments to the laws of a general interest to brokers and property owners, and which are of a non-technical nature. says:

The Department in its "instructions to applicants for licenses," 

"NOTE: IT IS UNLAWFUL FOR ANY PERSON TO EN- GAGE IN THE BUSINESS, ADVERTISE OR ASSUME TO ACT AS A REAL ESTATE BROKER OR SALESMAN IN CALIFORNIA UNTIL HE ACTUALLY HAS HIS LICENSE IN HIS POSSESSION. 

Merely filing an application or taking an examination does not permit him to operate. "Before being permitted to take the examination, applicants for original real estate broker or salesman licenses must file a completed application, together with the proper license and examination fees, at the Sacramento office or one of the branch offices of the State 

Real Estate Division. ALL FEES ARE PAYABLE AT THE TIME OF FILING LICENSE APPLICATION. DO NOT SEND PER- 

SONAL CHECKS. Personal checks will delay action on the application or examination at least two weeks. 

"WHEN COMPLETED APLICATIONS HAVE BEEN FILED, AND LICENSE FEES REMITTED, APPLICANTS WILL BE NO- TIFIED BY MAIL WHEN AND WHERE THEY MAY TAKE THE EXAMINATION. 

LICENSE DATES 

"All Brokers' and Salesmen's Licenses are issued for a period of one year, beginning July 1st, and ending June 30th of the suc ceeding year, unless previously suspended, revoked or cancelled. "BROKERS: Broker applicants who are uncertain of their business address at the time of filing their application must furnish this information after they are notified they have passed the examination, and before a license can be issued. as: "Section 2, of the California Real Estate Law defines a broker "A real estate broker within the meaning of this Act is a person, copartnership or corporation who, for a compensation, sells or offers for sale, buys, or offers to buy, lists, or solicits for prospective purchasers, or negotiates the purchase or sale or exchange of real estate, or who, for compensation, negotiates loans on real estate, leases, or offers to lease, or negotiates the sale, purchase, or exchange of leases, rents, or places for rent, or collects rent from real estate, or improvements thereon, for another or others.' 

"BROKERS EXAMINATION FEE: $15.00; LICENSE FEE: 

$5.00; TOTAL FEE; $20.00 CASH. -10

"In addition to the property owner recommendations provided for in the application, broker applicants must also file with their application and fees three letters of recommendation from representative business men in the community in which they intend to engage in business. “SALESMEN: Applicants for a salesman's license must file application accompanied by license fee of $2.00, examination fee of $3.00, total $5.00. The application must be filled out completely, all questions being answered and certificate of the employing broker must be signed. Applicants will be notified by the Division of Real 

Estate when and where to appear for the examination. "A real estate salesman is defined as 'one who for a compensation is employed by a licensed broker' to do any of the things covered by the broker's license. 

"BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES: The 1937 Legislature enacted a law entitled 'California Business Opportunity Act,' which became effective August 27th, 1937. This law requires those handling Business Opportunities to secure a license. Applicants for both forms of license must qualify by passing a written examination. act now incorporated in Real Estate Law. This Generally speaking, the laws, regulations and fees governing the operations under the California Business Opportunity Act, are the same as those governing the operations under the California Real Estate Law, except that fee for Salesman's examination under this act is $7.50.

Examinations for Business Opportunity Brokers and Salesmen, differ from the examination for Real Estate Brokers and Salesmen only in that they cover questions involving the "Alcoholic Beverage Control Act," and the rules and regulations governing the same; the "California Sales Tax Act" of 1933, and the methods of procedure thereunder; Personal Property Laws and a knowledge of 

Chattel Mortgages and Forms; and the Civil Code covering recording notice of intended sales, etc.

Complete information and sample examination for "Business 

Opportunities" will be found in Section XIV.

The Real Estate Law specifically states that performance of "one act, for a compensation" "shall constitute the person, co-partnership or corporation a real estate broker or salesman within the meaning of this Act." 

Examinations are given at a time and place designated by the Commissioner. Permission to take examination is issued from the 

Sacramento office, after receipt of application for license, accompanied by fee for both license and examination. For the past year or so, examinations in Los Angeles have been held on Saturday mornings, starting at 9 o'clock.

Three hours are allowed applicants to complete examination. 

At the expiration of this time examination papers must be turned in whether or not the applicant has finished. 

Four types of questions are used in both Broker and Salesmen's examinations: 

1. The "True" and "False" statement form, in which a state- -11-

ment is made, followed by the letters "T" and "F". Such questions are answered merely by encircling the letter "T" or "F" to indicate whether the statement is a true or false one. 

2. The direct answer type of question, in which the question is asked and the applicant phrases his own answer to it. 

3. The multiple choice type of question, in which a statement is made and four answers given. Three of the answers will be wrong, one correct. The applicant must place an "X" opposite the answer that he believes to be correct. 

4. Land measurements. There will be three questions on land measurements. A legal description of the land will be given, and the applicant must draw on a township plat, the outline of the land described, figure the acreage, and fill in the answer opposite the question.

Subject to change without notice in Department regulations, examinations usually consist of approximately 50 "true and false" questions in the Salesmen's Examination and 100 in the Broker's 

Examination. 

A mark of 75% passes.

Portions of the examination have weights as follows: 

True and False statements 

Fill in questions 

Multiple choice questions

Land measurements . 

DEPARTMENTAL WARNINGS 

50% 20% 20% 10% 

The Department cautions applicants against the following errors, which frequently delay the issuance of permission to take, examinations: 

1. Sending personal checks. These must be cleared before action can be taken. 

2. Failure to sign application. 

3. Failure to file three letters of recommendation in addition to recommendations required on the application proper. (Brokers only.) 

4. Failure to answer all questions. 

5. In case of salesmen, failure to have employing broker sign. 

6. Failure to give complete record of law violations. 

7. Furnishing name of employing broker incorrectly. 

8. Giving employing broker's address incorrectly (this must correspond to Department records). 

9. Illegible handwriting. 

10. Incomplete address.

RULES FOR EXAMINATION 

"Section 9 of the California Real Estate Law requires the Commissioner to ascertain by written examination that applicants have a knowledge of the following subjects: (a) The English language 

--Reading, Writing, Spelling; (b) Elementary Arithmetic; (c) Fair understanding of rudimentary principles of real estate conveyancing; (d) General purposes and legal effect of Deeds, Mortgages, -12-

Land Contracts of Sale and Leases; (e) The elementary principles of land economics and appraisals; (f) The obligations between principal and agent; (g) The principles of real estate Practice and 

Ethics; (h) The provisions of the California Real Estate Law. "The use of notes, of the California Real Estate Law, or aid of any kind during the course of the examination is forbidden and will result in a rating of zero for the offender. The use of unfair methods during the examination will be considered sufficient proof of the applicant's unfitness for license. "Applicants must provide their own pen and ink. "Licenses will be mailed from Sacramento to applicants who pass the examination. Those who fail will be notified when and where they may take a subsequent examination. 

'Applicants failing to pass must wait 30 days for re-examination. Applicants failing the second test must wait 60 days. 

Applicants who fail three or more times must wait 90 days between examinations."

TEST QUESTIONS FOR BROKERS 

Before proceeding with the study of the questions which follow, applicants for broker licenses will find it interesting to see how many of the following questions they can answer correctly. 

In the summer of 1937, the following article appeared in the California Real Estate Magazine; in a subsequent issue the accom. panying answers were given: 

Just so that veteran brokers may check up on themselves, the . real estate commissioner has furnished the following list of questions which are similar to those used in Section 2 of the real estate broker examination. This particular section counts for 20% of the possible 100% grade. Test your ability by answering the following: 

Q. A broker in Modesto wrote to a broker in San Francisco, stating that he wished to exchange some grazing land for a city income property. He described the land as follows: The SE¼ of the NW14 of the NW4 of Section 6; and the W½ of the SW14 of Sec. 5; and the N2 of the NW14 of Sec. 8, T. 7S., R 16 E., M. D. B. & M. (Mt. Diablo Base & Meridian). (a) How many acres were described? (b) Is all the land contiguous? (c) In what part of the state is the land located? 

A. a, 170; b, No; c, Central.

Q. A ranch owner encumbered his property with a mortgage, securing a note for $32,750.00, to run for 6 years. The annual interest rate specified on the loan was 42% for the first 3 years, and 

62% for the last 3 years. (a) What was the amount of each quarterly interest payment during the first 3 years? (b) During the last 3 years? (c) What was the total amount of interest paid during the 6 year terms? -13-

A. (a) $32,750.00 @ 42% per annum-$1,473.75. 14-$368.44. (b) $32,750.00 @ 62% per annum-$2,128.75. 1/4-$532.19. (c) $1,473.75 per year for 3 years-$4,421.25 $2,128.75 per year for 3 years-$6,386.25 

Total interest for 6 years— $10,807.50

Q. Which of the following words are spelled incorrectly: apoint, authorization, princapal, neccessary, cancelation, situation, acknowledgment, recordation, asign, homested, required, constitute. 

A. The following were misspelled: Appoint, principal, necessary, cancellation, assign and homestead. 

Q. A lot, fully improved with an apartment house produces an average net annual income of $7,250 after all expenses and depreciation is allowed. The apartments are rented unfurnished, and the income level of the district remains constant. What is the approximate value of the property, based upon capitalization of the net income? -14-

Q. How may recorded easements against land be released from the records?

A. They may be released by recording a suitable quit claim deed executed by the owner of the easement. 

Q. When do taxes become a lien on real property? 

A. At noon on the first Monday in March of each year. 

Q. From what date are taxes usually prorated in escrow? 

A. July 1st. 

Q. What is meant by "economic or ground rent"?

A. It is the residual rent attributable to the earnings of the land itself after fair allowance has been made for the chargeable expenses of the improvements and the fair rate of interest allowed for the money invested in the improvements. 

Q. How would you proceed to secure ejectment of a tenant who refuses to pay his rent?

A. Briefly, the owner may serve a three day notice to pay rent or quit. If the tenant refuses to comply, the owner may bring court action to secure judgment for the rent owed and for possession of the property. If judgment is secured, the sheriff will evict. (Refer to O.P.A. Rulings during war time.) 

Q. John Jones, broker, had an agreement with all his salesmen that they were to receive 55% of all commissions earned by them, provided, however, that if the salesman who made the sale did not also secure the listing, then the salesman who secured the listing was to receive 15% of the total commission, which was deductable from the commission of the salesman making the sale. 

In event salesman "A" listed a property for $27,500.00 and salesman "B" sold it and secured 5% commission for the broker, what commission would "A" receive? What was "B's" share? 

Commission 5% of $27,500.00 is $1,375.00. A. 

A gets 15% of $1,375.00 or $206.25. 

B gets 40% of $1,375.00 or $550.00.

Q. Name three instances when it might be desirable to bring suit to quiet title.

A. Default of recorded land contract; release of an encumbrance recorded through error; release of expired easement. 

Q. What is meant by the "straight line" method of allowing for depreciation?

A. Under this method the life of the building is estimated and the number of years of estimated life is divided into the cost of the improvements. The resulting figure is allowable annually for depreciation.

Q. In connection with a note, what is meant by a "holder in due course"?

A. A holder in due course is a holder in good faith, or a bonafide holder. He has taken the note in its complete and regular form, without its being in default, and for a valuable consideration. —15—

Section II CALIFORNIA REAL ESTATE LAW AS COMPILED BY LEGISLATIVE COUNSEL IN EFFECT AUGUST 4, 1943 CHAPTER 127 

An act to add Division 4 and Parts 1 and 2 thereof, comprising Sections 10000 to 11020, inclusive, and Section 30042 to the Business and Professions Code, thereby consolidating and revising the law supervised, administered and enforced by the State Division of Real Estate of the Department of Investment regulating transactions affecting interests in real or personal property, licensing brokers and salesmen with respect to dealings in real or personal property, imposing disciplinary and criminal penalties for the violation thereof and repealing acts and parts of acts specified therein. 

[Approved by Governor April 13, 1943. Filed with Secretary of State 

April 13, 1943.1

The people of the State of California do enact as follows: 

Section 1. Division and Parts 1 and 2 thereof, comprising 

Sections 10000 to 11020, inclusive, are added to the Business and Professions Code, to read: 

DIVISION 4. REAL ESTATE PART 1. 

LICENSING OF PERSONS CHAPTER 1. GENERAL PROVISIONS 

10000. This part may be cited as the Real Estate Law. 

10001. The definitions in this chapter apply to the provisions of this part only and do not affect any other provisions of this code. 

10002. "Board" refers to the Real Estate Board. 10003. 10004. 10005. "Commissioner" refers to the Real Estate Commissioner. "Department" refers to the Department of Investment. "Division" refers to the State Real Estate Division in the Department of Investment. 10006. and firm. "Person" includes copartnership, corporation, company 10007. "Provisions of this part relating to real estate" refers to the provisions of Chapters 1, 2, 3 and 6 of Part 1. 

10008. "Provisions of this part relating to business opportunity regulation" refers to the provisions of Chapters 1, 2, 4 and 6 of 

Part 1. 

10009. "Provisions of this part relating to cemetery brokerage" 

refers to the provisions of Chapters 1, 2, 5 and 6 of Part 1. 

10010.

"Provisions of this part relating to hearings" refers to the provisions of Article 3 of Chapter 2 of Part 1. 

10011. "Licensee," when used without modification, refers to a person, whether broker or salesman, licensed under any of the provisions of this part. 

10012. "Broker," when used without modification, refers to a person licensed as a broker under any of the provisions of this part. 

10013. "Salesman," when used without modification, refers to a person licensed as a salesman under any of the provisions of this part. 

10014. "Real estate licensee" refers to a person, whether broker or salesman, licensed under Chapter 3 of this part. 

10015. "Real estate broker" refers to a person licensed as a broker under Chapter 3 of this part. 

10016. "Real estate salesman" refers to a person licensed as a salesman under Chapter 3 of this part. 

10017. "Business opportunity licensee" refers to a person, whether broker or salesman, licensed under Chapter 4 of this part. 

10018. "Business opportunity broker" refers to a person licensed as a broker under Chapter 4 of this part. 

10019. "Business opportunity salesman" refers to a person licensed as a salesman under Chapter 4 of this part. 

10020. "Cemetery brokerage licensee" refers to a person, whether broker or salesman, licensed under Chapter 5 of this part. 

10021. "Cemetery broker" refers to a person licensed as a broker under Chapter 5 of this part. 

10022. "Cemetery salesman" refers to a person licensed as salesman under Chapter 5 of this part. 10023. "Mineral, oil and gas licensee" refers to a person, whether broker or salesman licensed under Chapter 7 of this part. 

10024. "Mineral, oil and gas broker" refers to a person licensed as a broker under Chapter 7 of this part. 

10025. "Mineral, oil and gas salesman" refers to a person licensed as a salesman under Chapter 7 of this part. -16-

CHAPTER 2. 

ADMINISTRATION Article 1. The Real Estate Board 

10050. There is in the Department of Investment a State Real Division 

Estate Division, the chief officer of which division is the Real Estate Commissioner. 

10051. There is a Real Estate Board which consists of the Real 

Estate Commissioner and six other members.

All members of the board shall be appointed by the Governor. 

10052. Members of the board shall be appointed for a term of four years and they shall hold office until the appointment and qualification of their successors. 

The terms of the members of the board in office when this section takes effect shall expire as follows: One member, January 15, 1944; two members, January 15, 1945; two members, January 15, 1946; and two members, including the Real Estate Commissioner, January 

15, 1947.

The terms shall expire in the same relative order as to each member as the term for which he holds office before this section takes effect.

Vacancies from any cause shall be filled by the Governor for the unexpired term. 

10053. No person shall be appointed a member of the board who has not been for five years a real estate broker actively engaged in business as such in California. and board created 

Terms of board members 10054. Three members of the board shall be residents of the Districts northern district of California, and three members shall be residents appointed of the southern district of California. The commissioner shall be from appointed at large. Not more than two members shall be appointed from any one county.

The northern district shall consist of all that portion of the State north of the northerly lines of the counties of San Luis Obispo, Kern and San Bernardino, and the southern district shall consist of all that portion of the State south of the northerly lines of these three counties. 

10055. Each member of the board, except the commissioner, shall Compensaserve without compensation. tion The commissioner shall receive an annual salary of seven thousands five hundred dollars ($7,500), to be paid monthly out of the 

State treasury upon a warrant of the Controller.

Each member shall be allowed his actual and necessary traveling expenses in the discharge of his duties. 

10056. The board shall meet together for the transaction of Board business at least once each quarter-year, at such place in California meetings as it may designate. It may meet more often upon five days' written notice of the time and place of meeting, signed by the commissioner or a majority of the members of the board. 

10057. The commissioner shall be chairman of the board. 

10058. A majority of the board constitutes a quorum for the Quorum transaction of any business, for the performance of any duty, or for the exercise of any power or authority of the board. 

A vacancy on the board does not impair the right of the remaining members to perform all the duties and exercise all the power and authority of the board. 

The act of the majority of the board, when in session as a board, is the act of the board. 

10059. The board may: (a) Inquire into the needs of the real estate licensees of Cali- Functions fornia, the functions of the division and the matter of the business of board policy thereof. (b) Confer and advise with the Governor and other State officers as to how the division may best serve the State and the real estate licensees of the division. (c) Make such recommendations and suggestions of policy to the commissioner as the board deems beneficial and proper for the welfare and progress of the real estate licensees and of the public and of the real estate business in California.

Article 2. The Real Estate Commissioner 

10070. The Real Estate Commissioner shall be the representative of the State Real Estate Division in the Department of Investment for the purpose of representation in the Governor's Council. -17-

10073. The commissioner shall employ such deputies, clerks and employees as he may need to discharge in proper manner the duties imposed upon him by law. 

10074. After qualifying as such, neither the commissioner nor any of the deputies, clerks or employees of the division shall be interested in any business opportunity company, business opportunity brokerage firm, cemetery business, cemetery brokerage firm, real estate company or any real estate brokerage firm, as director, stockholder, officer, member, agent or employee, or act as a broker or salesman, or act as a copartner or agent for any broker or brokers, salesman or salesmen.

Subject to the powers of the State Personnel Board and the Director of Finance, the commissioner shall fix the compensation of such deputies, clerks and employees, which compensation shall be paid monthly on a certificate of the commissioner, and on the warrant of the Controller out of the State Treasury.

Article 3. Hearings 

10100. Before denying, suspending or revoking any license issua- Disciplinble or issued under the provisions of this part, the commissioner ary shall proceed as prescribed by this article. procedure 10101. In case a hearing is called on an application for a broker's Temporary license, the commissioner, upon the request of the applicant, and licenses upon the payment of the additional temporary broker's license fee shall issue a temporary broker's license in accordance with that chapter of this part under which the application held an unrevoked or unsuspended license on June 30th of the preceding fiscal year as an individual broker, a corporation, an officer of a corporation, a copartnership or member of a copartnership. The temporary broker's license shall expire at the time the decision rendered by the commissioner takes effect. 

10102. In case a hearing is called on an application for a salesman's license, the commissioner, upon the request of the applicant, accompanied by the recommendation of the broker under whom the salesman is seeking a license, and upon the payment of the additional temporary salesman's license fee, shall issue a temporary salesman's license in accordance with that chapter of this part under which the applicant held an unrevoked or unsuspended salesman's or broker's license on June 30th of the preceding fiscal year. 

The temporary salesman's license shall expire at the time the decision rendered by the commissioner takes effect. 

10103. The commissioner shall notify, in writing, the applicant or licensee of the charges against him and afford him an opportunity to be heard in person or by counsel with reference to the charges. 

Service upon the licensee or applicant of the charges against him or of the notice of the time and place of trial shall be fully effected by mailing a true copy of the charges or notice by United States registered mail in a sealed envelope with postage fully prepaid thereon to the licensee or applicant at his latest address of record in the division. Within 10 days after service of a copy of the charges, the accused licensee or applicant shall appear and file a verified answer to the charges. 

10104. In suspending or revoking any license, or in denying any application for a license where the applicant is the holder of a temporary license, either as a broker or salesman, the decision of the commissioner shall not take effect until 10 days after its date. 

When revocation takes effect 10105. The decision of the commissioner in denying, suspending Review of or revoking any license is subject to judicial review in accordance decision with law. 

10106. Any party aggrieved by the decision of the commissioner may make a demand in writing for a certified transcript of all the papers on file in his office affecting or relating to such decision and all the evidence taken on the hearing and paying ten cents ($0.10) for each folio of the transcript and one dollar ($1) for the certification thereof. Thereupon the commissioner shall, within 30 days, make and certify such transcript. -19-

Powers of commis- sioner

Service of process

Witness fees 

Powers of superior court Attendance of wit- nesses Depositions

Right of attendance of wit- nesses License required 10107. The commissioner may administer oaths, certify to all official acts and issue subpoenas for the attendance of witnesses and the production of books and papers. 

10108. In any hearing in any part of the State the process issued by the commissioner shall extend to all parts of the State and may be served by any person authorized to serve process of courts of record or by any person designated for that purpose by the commissioner. 

10109. The person serving any process issued by the commissloner shall receive such compensation as may be allowed by the commissioner, not to exceed the fees prescribed by law for similar service. The fees shall be paid in the same manner as provided in this article for the payment of the fees of witnesses. 

10110. Each witness who appears by order of the commissioner shall receive for his attendance the same fees and mileage allowed by law to a witness in civil cases, which amount shall be paid by the party at whose request the witness is subpoenaed. 

10111. When any witness who has not been required to attend at the request of any party is subpoenaed by the commissioner his fees and mileage shall be paid from the funds appropriated for the use of the division in the same manner as other expenses of the division are paid. 

10112. The superior court in and for the county in which any hearing may be held by the commissioner may compel the attendance of witnesses, the giving of testimony and the production of books and papers as required by any subpoena issued by the commissioner. 

10113. In case of the refusal of any witness to attend or testify or produce any papers required by such subpoena, the commissioner may petition the superior court in and for the county in which the hearing is pending, setting forth: (a) That due notice has been given to the witness of the time and place of attendance or for the production of papers. (b) That the witness has been summoned in the manner prescribed in this article. (c) That the witness has failed and refused to attend or produce the papers required by subpoena before the commissioner in the cause or proceeding named in the subpoena, or has refused to answer questions propounded to him in the course of the hearing. (d) A request for an order of court compelling the witness to attend and testify or produce the papers before the commissioner. 

10114. The court upon petition of the commissioner shall enter an order directing the witness to appear before the court at a time and place to be fixed by the court in its order, the time to be not more than 10 days from the date of the order, and then and there show cause why he has not attended or testified or produced the papers before the commissioner. A copy of the order shall be served upon the witness. 

If it shall appear to the court that the subpoena was regularly issued by the commissioner, the court shall thereupon enter an order that the witness appear before the commissioner at the time and place fixed in the order and testify or produce the required papers, and upon failure to obey the order, the witness shall be dealt with as for contempt of court. 

10115. The commissioner may in any hearing before him cause the deposition of witnesses residing within or without the State to be taken in the manner prescribed by law for like depositions in civil actions in the superior courts of this State, and to that end may compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of books and papers. 

10116. Any party to any hearing before the commissioner shall have the right to the attendance of witnesses in his behalf at such hearing or upon deposition upon making request therefor to the commissioner and designating the person or persons sought to be subpoenaed.

CHAPTER 3. 

REAL ESTATE REGULATIONS Article 1. Scope of Regulation 

10130. It is unlawful for any person to engage in the business, act in the capacity of, advertise or assume to act as a real estate broker or a real estate salesman within this State without first obtaining a real estate license from the division. 

The commissioner may prefer a complaint for violation of this section before any court of competent jurisdiction, and the commissioner and his counsel, deputies or assistants may assist in presenting the law or facts at the trial. -20

10131. A real estate broker within the meaning of this part is a Broker person who, for a compensation, sells or offers for sale, buys, or defined offers to buy, lists, or solicits for prospective purchasers, or negotiates the purchase or sale or exchange of real estate, or who, for compensation, negotiates loans on real estate, leases, or offers to lease, or negotiates the sale, purchase, or exchange of leases, rents, or places for rent, or collects rent from real estate, or improvements thereon, for another or others. Salesman 10132. A real estate salesman within the meaning of this part is a natural person who for a compensation is employed by a licensed defined real estate broker to sell, or offer for sale, or to list, or to buy, or to offer to buy, or to negotiate the purchase or sale or exchange of real estate, or to solicit for prospective purchasers of real estate, or to negotiate a loan on real estate, or to lease, or to negotiate the sale, purchase or exchange of leases, or offer to lease, rent or place for rent, any real estate, or improvements thereon. 

10133. The provisions of this chapter, except Section 10140, do Application not apply to: of law (a) Anyone who directly performs any of the acts within the scope of this chapter with reference to his own property or, in the case of a corporation which, through its regular officers receiving no special compensation therefor, performs any of the acts with reference to the corporation's own property. owner. (b) Anyone holding a duly executed power of attorney from the (c) Services rendered by an attorney at law in performing his duties as such attorney at law. (d) Any receiver, trustee in bankruptcy, or any person acting under order of any court. (e) Any trustee selling under a deed of trust. 

10134. One act, for a compensation of buying or selling real estate of or for another, or offering for another to buy or sell or exchange real estate, or negotiating the purchase or sale or exchange of, or listing or soliciting prospective purchasers of real estate, or negotiating a loan on or leasing or renting or placing for rent real estate, or collecting rent therefrom constitutes the person making such offer, sale or purchase, exchange or lease, or negotiating the loan, or so renting or placing for rent or collecting the rent or listing or soliciting, a real estate broker or real estate salesman within the meaning of this part. 

One act constitutes person, etc. broker or salesman 10135. When a lease or leasing is referred to in this article, Leasing it includes any lease, whether such lease is the sole transaction involved, or the principal or an incidental part of the transaction involved. 

10136. No person engaged in the business or acting in the Action for capacity of a real estate broker or a real estate salesman within compensathis State shall bring or maintain any action in the courts of this tion State for the collection of compensation for the performance of any of the acts mentioned in this article without alleging and proving that he was a duly licensed real estate broker or real estate salesman at the time the alleged cause of action arose. 

10137. It is unlawful for any licensed real estate broker to employ or compensate, directly or indirectly, any person for performing any of the acts within the scope of this chapter who is not a licensed real estate broker, or a real estate salesman licensed under sation the broker employing or compensating him. 

No real estate salesman shall be employed by or accept compensation from any person other than the broker under whom he is at the time licensed.

It is unlawful for any licensed real estate salesman to pay any compensation for performing any of the acts within the scope of this chapter to any real estate licensee except through the broker under whom he is at the time licensed.

For a violation of any of the provisions of this section, the commissioner may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke the license of the real estate licensee, in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings. 

10138. It is a misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of not exceeding fifty dollars ($50) for each offense, for any person, whether obligor, escrow holder or otherwise, to pay or deliver to anyone a compensation for performing any of the acts within the scope of this chapter, who is not known to be or who does not present evi- Unlawful payment of compen- -21-

Violations

Penalties dence to such payor that he is a regularly licensed real estate broker at the time such compensation is earned. 

For violation of any of the provisions of this section, the commissioner may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke the license of the real estate licensee in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings. 

10139. Any person acting as a real estate broker or real estate salesman without a license or who advertises using words indicating that he is a real estate broker without being so licensed shall, upon conviction thereof, if a natural person, be punished by a fine of not to exceed five hundred dollars ($500), or by imprisonment in the county jail for a term not to exceed six months, or by both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court; or if a corporation, be punished by a fine of not to exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000). 

10140. Every officer, agent or employee or any company, and every other person who knowingly authorizes, directs or aids in the publication, advertisement, distribution or circularization of any false statement or representation concerning any land or subdivision thereof (as defined in Chapter 1 of Part 2 of this division), offered for sale or lease, and every person who, with knowledge that any advertisement, pamphlet, prospectus or letter concerning any said land or subdivision (as defined in Chapter 1 of Part 2 of this division) contains any written statement that is false or fraudulent, issues, circulates, publishes or distributes the same, or causes the same to be issued, circulated, published or distributed, or who, in any other respect, wilfully violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this section, or who in any other respect wilfully violates or fails, omits or neglects to obey, observe or comply with any order, permit, decision, demand or requirement of the commissioner under this section, is guilty of a public offense, and shall be punished by imprisonment in the county jail for a term not to exceed two years, by a fine of not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), and, if a real estate licensee, he shall be held to trial by the commissioner for a suspension or revocation of his license, as provided in the provisions of this part relating to hearings. The district attorney of each county in this State shall prosecute all violations of the provisions of this section in respective counties in which the violations occur.

The commissioner may, at his discretion, waive the examination Salesman's of any applicant for a real estate salesman's license who held an unrevoked or unsuspended real estate salesman's license on June 30th of the preceding fiscal year and who had previously qualified by passing the written examination. 

10157. No real estate license gives authority to do any act specified in this chapter to any person, other than the person to whom the license is issued.

When a real estate license is issued to a corporation, Corporaif it desires any of its officers other than its president, to act under tion and its license as a real estate broker, it shall procure an additional partnerlicense to so employ each of such officers. When a real estate ship license license is granted to a copartnership, if it desires any of its members other than the one or ones through whom it is already licensed to act as a real estate broker, it shall procure an additional license to 80 employ each of such additional members. 

10159. Each officer of a corporation through whom it is licensed to act as a real estate broker, and each member of a copartnership through whom it is licensed to act as a real estate broker, is, while so employed under such license, a licensed real estate broker, but licensed only to act as such for and on behalf of the corporation or the copartnership, as officer or member, respectively. 10160. Immediately upon the real estate salesman's withdrawal from the employ of the real estate broker, the real estate broker shall return the real estate salesman's license to the commissioner for cancellation. A license canceled but not suspended or revoked may be reinstated within the fiscal year upon receipt of application therefor and the fee for the reinstatement of his license. -23

Definite office required

Change of business location

Display of sign 10162. Every licensed real estate broker shall have and maintain a definite place of business in the State of California which shall serve as his office for the transaction of business. 

No real estate license authorizes the licensee to do business except from the location stipulated in the real estate license. 

Notice in writing shall be given the commissioner of change of business location of a real estate broker, whereupon the commissioner shall issue a new license for the unexpired period. The change or abandonment of business location without notification to the commissioner and the issuance by him of a new real estate license shall automatically cancel the license theretofore issued. 

10163. If the applicant for a real estate broker's license maintains more than one place of business within the State he shall apply for and procure an additional license for each branch office so maintained by him. Every such application shall state the name of the person and the location of the place or places of business for which such license is desired. The commissioner may determine whether or not a real estate broker is doing a real estate brokerage business at or from any particular location which requires him to have a branch office license. 

10164. Each real estate broker shall erect and maintain a sign in a conspicuous place on the premises to indicate that he is a licensed real estate broker and his name shall be clearly shown thereon. The size and place of the sign shall conform to regulations that may be adopted by the commissioner. 

10165. For a violation of any of the provisions of Sections 10160, 10161, 10162, and 10164, the commissioner may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke the license of the real estate licensee in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings. 

Article 3. Disciplinary Action 

10175. Upon grounds provided in this article and the other articles of this chapter, the license of any real estate licensee may be revoked or suspended in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings.

Grounds for 10176. The commissioner may, upon his own motion, and shall disciplinary upon the verified complaint in writing of any person, investigate action the actions of any person engaged in the business or acting in the capacity of a real estate licensee within this State, and he may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke a real estate license at any time where the licensee within the immediately preceding three years, while a real estate licensee, in performing or attempting to perform any of the acts within the scope of this chapter has been guilty of any of the following:

Additional grounds (a) Making any substantial misrepresentation. (b) Making any false promises of a character likely to influence, persuade or induce. (c) A continued and flagrant course of misrepresentation or making of false promises through real estate agents or salesmen. (d) Acting for more than one party in a transaction without the knowledge or consent of all parties thereto. (e) Commingling the money or other property of his principal with his own. (f) Any other conduct, whether of the same or a different character than specified in this section, which constitutes fraud or dishonest dealing. 

10177. The commissioner may suspend or revoke the license of any real estate licensee, who within three years immediately preceding has done any of the following: (a) Procured a real estate license, for himself or any salesman, by fraud, misrepresentation or deceit. (b) Been convicted of a felony, knowledge of which the commissioner did not have at the time of last issuing a real estate license to him. (c) Knowingly authorized, directed, connived at or aided in the publication, advertisement, distribution, or circulation of any material false statement or representation concerning his business or any land or subdivision (as defined in Chapter 1 of Part 2 of this division) offered for sale. (d) Wilfully disregarded or violated any of the provisions of this part relating to real estate or of Chapter 1 of Part 2. 

(e) Wilfully used the term "realtor" without legal right so to do. (f) Acted or conducted himself in a manner which would have warranted the denial of his application for a real estate license, or for a renewal thereof. -24-

Article 4. Fees 

10200. The fee for all real estate licenses shall at all periods of the fiscal year be the same as provided in this article. All real estate license fees shall be payable in advance of issuing the licenses and all examination fees shall be payable before taking the examination.

Unless otherwise provided, all licenses expire on June 30th of Expiration each year at midnight. of licenses 10201. If a person fails to apply for a renewal of his real estate Renewals license prior to the date of expiration thereof, no license shall be issued to him except upon another original application, except that within one year of such expiration, a renewal license may be issued upon payment of a fee double the amount otherwise required for Penalty renewal. 

10202. The definitions contained in this article are solely for the purposes of this article. 

10203. An original real estate broker's license is a real estate Broker license issued to a person who did not have a real estate broker's license license on June 30th of the fiscal year previous to the fiscal year for which the license is issued.

CHAPTER 4. BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY REGULATIONS Article 1. Scope of Regulation 

10250. It is unlawful for any person to engage in the business, act in the capacity of, or assume to act as a business opportunity broker or a business opportunity salesman within this State without first obtaining a license from the division. 

The commissioner may prefer a complaint for violation of this section before any court of competent jurisdiction, and the commissioner and his counsel, deputies or assistants may assist in presenting the law or facts at the trial. 

It is the duty of the district attorney of each county in this State to prosecute all violations of this section in their respective counties in which the violations occur. 

10251. As used in this part, the words "business opportunity" shall mean and include business, business opportunity and good will of an existing business or any one or combination thereof. 

10252. A business opporttunity broker within the meaning of this part is a person who, for a compensation, sells or offers for sale, rents, or offers to rent, or collects rent, buys, or offers to buy, lists, leases or offers to lease, or solicits for prospective tenants or purchasers, or negotiates the purchase or sale or the renting, leasing or exchanging of a business, business opportunity, or interest therein, or the good will of an existing business, for another or others. 

10253. A business opportunity salesman within the meaning of this part is a natural person who for a compensation is employed by a licensed business opportunity broker to sell, or offer for sale, to rent, or offer to rent, or collect rent, or to list or offer to list, or to buy, or to offer to buy, or to lease or offer to lease, or to solicit for prospective tenants or purchasers, or to negotiate the purchase or sale or the renting, leasing, or exchanging of a business, business opportunity, or interest therein, or the good will of an existing business. 

10254. The provisions of this chapter, except Section 10261, do not apply to: (a) Anyone who directly performs any of the acts within the scope of this chapter with reference to his own property or, in case of a corporation, through its regular officers receiving no special compensation therefor, performs any of the acts with reference to the corporation's own property. -26-

(b) Anyone holding a duly executed power of attorney from the owner. (c) Services rendered by an attorney at law in performing his duties as such attorney at law. (d) Any receiver, trustee in bankruptcy, or any person acting under order of any court. (e) A trustee selling under a deed of trust. (1) A real estate broker or real estate salesman while acting as such in connection with the sale, lease or exchange of real property or an interest therein when the transfer of a business, business opportunity or good will of an existing business is purely incidental to the sale, lease or exchange of real property. 

10255. One act, for a compensation of buying or selling a business opportunity of or for another, or offering for another to buy or sell or exchange a business opportunity, or negotiating the purchase or sale or exchange of, or listing or soliciting prospective purchasers of business opportunities, or negotiating a loan on or leasing or renting or placing for rent a business opportunity, or collecting rent therefrom constitutes the person making such offer, sale or purchase, exchange or lease, or negotiating the loan, or so renting or placing for rent or collecting the rent or listing or soliciting, a business opportunity broker or salesman within the meaning of this part. 

One act constitutes person, etc. broker or salesman 10256. When a lease or leasing is referred to in this article, it Lease includes any lease, whether such a lease is the sole transaction involved, or the principal or an incidental part of the transaction involved. 

10257. No person engaged in the business or acting in the Action for capacity of a business opportunity broker or a business opportunity compensasalesman within this State shall bring or maintain any action in tion the courts of this State for the collection of compensation for the performance of any of the acts mentioned in this article without alleging and proving that he was a duly licensed business opportunity broker or business opportunity salesman at the time the alleged cause of action arose. 

10258. It is unlawful for any licensed business opportunity No compen. broker to employ or compensate, directly or indirectly, any person sation to for performing any of the acts within the scope of this chapter who unlicensed is not a licensed business opportunity broker, or a business oppor- person tunity salesman licensed under the broker employing or compensating him.

No business opportunity salesman shall be employed by or accept compensation from any person other than the business opportunity broker under whom he is at the time licensed.

It is unlawful for any licensed business opportunity salesman to pay any compensation for performing any of the acts within the Scope of this chapter to any business opportunity licensee except through the business opportunity broker under whom he is at the time licensed.

For a violation of any of the provisions of this section, the commissioner may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke the license of the business opportunity licensee in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings. 

10259. It is a misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of not exceeding Misdefifty dollars ($50) for each offense, for any person, whether obligor, meanor escrow holder or otherwise, to pay or deliver to anyone a compensa- punishable tion for performing any of the acts within the scope of this chapter, by fine who is not known to be or who does not present evidence to such payor that he is a regularly licensed business opportunity broker at the time such compensation is earned.

(c) Knowingly authorized, directed, connived at or aided in the publication, advertisement, distribution or circulation of any material false statement or representation concerning his business or any business opportunity offered for sale. (d) Wilfully disregarded or violated any of the provisions of this part relating to business opportunity regulation. (e) Acted or conducted himself in a manner which would have warranted the denial of his application for a business opportunity license, or for a renewal thereof.

CHAPTER 5. 

CEMETERY BROKERAGE REGULATIONS Article 1. Scope of Regulation 

10350. No person shall engage in the business of, act in the License capacity of, advertise or assume to act as, a cemetery broker or required cemetery salesman in this State without first obtaining a license from the commissioner. 

10351. A cemetery broker is a person who, for a compensation, Broker sells or offers for sale, buys, or offers to buy, lists, leases or offers to lease, or solicits, or negotiates the purchase or sale, lease or exchange of cemetery property, or interest therein, for another. 

10352. A cemetery salesman is a natural person who for a com- Salesman pensation is employed by a cemetery broker to sell, or offer for sale, list or offer to list, or to buy, or to offer to buy, or to lease, or to offer to lease, or to solicit, or to negotiate the purchase or sale or lease or exchange of cemetery property, or any interest therein. -31-

10357. This chapter, except Section 10363, does not apply to the following cases or to the following persons: (a) A person acting with reference to his own property. (b) The regular officers of a cemetery corporation acting with reference to the corporation's property when they receive no special compensation therefor. (c) Persons holding a duly executed power of attorney from others. (d) The services rendered by an attorney at law in performing his duties as such. (e) A receiver, trustee in bankruptcy, any person acting under orders of any court, or a trustee selling under a deed of trust. (f) A real estate broker or real estate salesman, acting as such in connection with the sale, lease or exchange of real property, or interest therein, when the transfer of cemetery property is purely incidental to the sale, lease or exchange of real property. 

10358. Any act for a compensation of buying or selling, leasing or exchanging cemetery property of or for another, or offering for another to buy or sell, lease or exchange cemetery property, or negotiating the purchase or sale, lease or exchange of cemetery property, or negotiating the purchase or sale, lease or exchange of, or listing or soliciting, or negotiating a loan on or leasing of cemetery property constitutes the person making such offer, sale or purchase, exchange or lease, or negotiating the loan, or listing or soliciting, a cemetery broker or a cemetery salesman. 

10359. No person engaged in the business or acting in the capacity of a broker or a salesman within this State shall bring or maintain any action in the courts of this State for the collection of compensation for the performance of any of the acts mentioned in this article without alleging and proving that he was a duly licensed cemetery broker or cemetery salesman at the time the alleged cause of action arose.

10385. Immediately upon the salesman's withdrawal from the employ of the broker, the broker shall return the salesman's license to the commissioner for cancellation. A license cancelled but not suspended or revoked may be reinstated within the fiscal year upon receipt of application therefor and the fee for the reinstatement of his license. 

10386. Every licensed cemetery broker shall have and maintain a definite place of business in this State which shall serve as his office for the transaction of business.

No cemetery license authorizes the licensee to do business except from the location stipulated in the cemetery license. 

Notice in writing shall be given the commissioner of change of business location of a cemetery broker, whereupon the commissioner shall issue a new cemetery license for the unexpired period. The change or abandonment of business location without notification to the commissioner and the issuance by him of a new cemetery license shall automatically cancel the license theretofore issued. 

10387. If the applicant for a cemetery broker's license maintains more than one place of business within the State he shall apply for and procure an additional license for each branch office so maintained by him. Every such application shall state the name of the person and the location of the place of business for which such license is desired.

The commissioner may determine whether or not a broker is doing a cemetery brokerage business at or from any particular location which requires him to have a branch office license. 

10388. Each cemetery broker shall erect and maintain a sign in a conspicuous place on the premises to indicate that he is a licensed cemetery broker and his name shall be clearly shown thereon. The size and place of the sign shall conform to regulations that may be adopted by the commissioner. 

10389. For a violation of any of the provisions of Sections 10384, 10385, 10386, and 10388, the commissioner may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke the license of the cemetery licensee in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings. -34-

Article 3. Disciplinary Action 

10400. Upon grounds provided in this article and the other articles of this chapter, the license of any cemetery licensee may be revoked or suspended in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings. 

10401. The commissioner may, upon his own motion, and shall, Suspension upon the verified complaint in writing of any person, investigate and revoca. the actions of any person engaged in the business or acting in the tion of capacity of a cemetery licensee, and he may temporarily suspend or licenses permanently revoke a license at any time where the licensee, within the immediately preceding three years, while a cemetery licensee, in performing or attempting to perform any of the acts specified in this chapter, has been guilty of any of the following: (a) Making any substantial misrepresentation. (b) Making any false statement of a character likely to influence or persuade. (c) A continued and flagrant course of misrepresentation or making of false promises through cemetery agents or salesmen. (d) Acting for more than one party in a transaction without the knowledge or consent of all parties thereto. (e) Commingling the money or other property of his principal with his own. (f) Any other conduct, whether of the same or a different character than specified in this section, which constitutes fraud or dishonest dealing.

The misrepresentations and false statements mentioned in this section include also misrepresentation and false statements as to other property than that which the cemetery licensee may be selling or attempting to sell. 

10402. The commissioner may suspend or revoke the license Other of any cemetery licensee who, within three years immediately pre- grounds of ceding has done any of the following: action (a) Procured a cemetery license, for himself or any salesman, by fraud, misrepresentation or deceit. (b) Been convicted of a felony, knowledge of which the commissioner did not have at the time of last issuing a cemetery license to him. (c) Knowingly authorized, directed, connived at or aided in the publication, advertisement, distribution, or circulation of any material false statement or representation concerning his business or any cemetery property offered for sale. (d) Wilfully disregarded or violated any of the provisions of this part relating to cemetery brokerage. (e) Acted or conducted himself in a manner which would have warranted the denial of his application for a cemetery license, or for a renewal thereof. 

10403. When any salesman is discharged by his employer for a Employer's violation of any of the provisions of this article prescribing a ground statements for disciplinary action, a verified written statement of the facts with reference thereto shall be filed forthwith with the commissioner by the employer and, if the employer fails to notify the commissioner as required by this section, the commissioner may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke the cemetery license of the employer in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings. 

10404. The commissioner may deny, suspend or revoke the cemetery license of a corporation as to any officer or agent acting under its cemetery license, and the cemetery license of a copartnership as to any member acting under its cemetery license, without revoking the cemetery license of the corporation or of the copartnership.

CHAPTER 749 

An act to amend Section 10074 of, to add Sections 10009.5, 10023, 10024, 10025 and 11011.5 to, and to add Chapter 7, comprising 

Sections 10500 to 10601, to Part 1 of Division 4 of, the Business and Professions Code, relating to transactions in mineral, oil or gas property, regulating mineral, oil and gas brokers and salesmen and prescribing the powers and duties of the State Division of Real Estate with respect thereto. 

[Approved by Governor May 26, 1943. Filed with Secretary of State 

May 26, 1943.]

The people of the State of California do enact as follows: 

CHAPTER 7. 

MINERAL, OIL ANG GAS BROKERAGE Article 1. Scope of Regulation 

10500. It is unlawful for any person to engage in the business, act in the capacity of, advertise or assume to act as a mineral, oil and gas broker or a mineral, oil and gas salesman within this State without first obtaining a mineral, oil and gas license from the division. 

The commissioner may prefer a complaint for violation of this section before any court of competent jurisdiction, and the commissioner and his counsel, deputies or assistants may assist in presenting the law or facts at the trial. 

It is the duty of the district attorney of each county in this State to prosecute all violations of this section in their respective counties in which the violations occur. 

10501. A mineral, oil and gas broker within the meaning of this part is a person who, for a compensation, sells or offers for sale, buys, or offers to buy, lists, or solicits for prospective purchasers, or negotiates the purchase or sale or exchange of mineral, oil or gas property, or who, for compensation, negotiates loans on mineral, oil or gas property, leases, or offers to lease, or negotiates the sale, purchase, or exchange of leases, rents, or places for rent, or collects rent or royalties from mineral, oil or gas property, for another or others. 

10502. A mineral, oil and gas salesman within the meaning of this part is a natural person who for a compensation is employed by a licensed mineral, oil and gas broker to sell, or offer for sale, or to list, or to buy, or to offer to buy, or to negotiate the purchase or sale or exchange of mineral, oil or gas property, or to solicit for prospective purchasers of mineral, oil or gas property, or to negotiate a loan on mineral, oil or gas property, or to lease, or to negotiate the sale, purchase or exchange of leases or offer to lease, rent or place for rent, any mineral, oil or gas property. 

10503. Mineral, oil or gas property refers to land used for, intended to be used for, or concerning which representations are made with respect to, the mining of minerals or the extraction of oil or gas therefrom. 

10504. Mineral, oil and gas broker within the meaning of this part includes any person who engages in the business of buying or leasing, or who takes an option on, mineral, oil or gas property, for the purpose of sale or resale, or lease or sublease, or assignment of a lease, or exchange, of such property or any part of such property. 

10505. The provisions of this chapter do not apply to: (a) Any person acting solely as a depositary under an oil or gas lease, or oil and gas lease, other than for purposes of sale. (b) Any person who engages in any transaction pursuant to an order of a court of competent jurisdiction. (c) Any person, and the officers and employees of such person, engaged in the business of drilling for or producing oil or gas, or of mining for or producing minerals. 

10506. One act, for a compensation of buying or selling a mineral, oil or gas property of or for another, or offering for another to buy or sell or exchange a mineral, oil or gas property, or negotiating the purchase or sale or exchange of, or listing or soliciting prospective purchasers of mineral, oil or gas property, or negotiating a loan on or leasing or renting or placing for rent a mineral, oil or gas property, or collecting rent therefrom constitutes the person making such offer, sale or purchase, exchange or lease, or negotiating the loan, or so renting or placing for rent or collecting the rent or listing or soliciting, a mineral, oil and gas broker or salesman within the meaning of this part. 

10507. (a) The provisions of this chapter, except Section 10512, do not apply to a real estate licensee while acting as such in connection with the sale, lease or exchange of real property (other -38-

than mineral, oil or gas property) or an interest therein, when the transfer of mineral, oil or gas property is purely incidental to the sale, lease or exchange of real property (other than mineral, oil or gas property). (b) Any real estate licensee, who performs an act or engages in a transaction subject to this chapter, which act or transaction is incidental to his real estate business but not within subdivision (a), may secure a permit for such act or transaction from the commissioner without otherwise complying with the provisions of this chapter, except Section 10512. Not more than 10 permits per fiscal year may be issued under this section to any real estate licensee. The real estate permit fee shall be paid for each permit. 

10508. No person engaged in the business or acting in the Action for capacity of a mineral, oil and gas broker or a mineral, oil and gas compensasalesman within this State shall bring or maintain any action in the tion courts of this State for the collection of compensation for the performance of any of the acts mentioned in this article without alleging and proving that he was a duly licensed mineral, oil and gas broker or mineral, oil and gas salesman at the time the alleged cause of action arose. 

10509. It is unlawful for any licensed mineral, oil and gas broker to employ or compensate, directly or indirectly, any person for performing any of the acts within the scope of this chapter who is not a licensed mineral, oil and gas broker, or a mineral, oil and gas salesman licensed under the broker employing or compensating him. 

No mineral, oil and gas salesman shall be employed by or accept compensation from any person other than the mineral, oil and gas broker under whom he is at the time licensed.

It is unlawful for any licensed mineral, oil and gas salesman to pay any compensation for performing any of the acts within the scope of this chapter to any mineral, oil and gas licensee except through the mineral, oil and gas broker under whom he is at the time licensed.

For a violation of any of the provisions of this section, the commissioner may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke the license of the mineral, oil and gas licensee in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings. Unlawful payment of compensa- tion 10510. It is a misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of not exceed Violations ing fifty dollars ($50) for each offense, for any person, whether obligor, escrow holder or otherwise, to pay or deliver to anyone a compensation for performing any of the acts within the scope of this chapter, who is not known to be or who does not present evidence to such payor that he is a regularly licensed mineral, oil and gas broker at the time such compensation is earned. 

For a violation of any of the provisions of this section, the commissioner may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke the license of the mineral, oil and gas licensee in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings. 

10511. Any person acting as a mineral, oil and gas broker or Penalties mineral, oil and gas salesman without a license shall, upon conviction thereof, if a natural person, be punished by a fine of not to exceed five hundred dollars ($500), or by imprisonment in the county jail for a term not to exceed six months, or by both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court; or if a corporation, be punished by a fine of not to exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000). 

10512. Every officer, agent or employee of any company, and every other person who knowingly authorizes, directs or aids in the publication, advertisement, distribution or circularization of any false statement or representation concerning any mineral, oil or gas property, and every person who, with knowledge that any advertisement, pamphlet, prospectus or letter concerning any mineral, oil or gas property or any written statement that is false or fraudulent, issues, circulates, publishes or distributes the same, or causes the same to be issued, circulated, published or distributed, or who in any other respect wilfully violates or fails, omits, or neglects to obey, observe or comply with any order, permit, decision, demand or requirement of the commissioner under the provisions of this part relating to mineral, oil and gas brokerage, is guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall be punished by imprisonment in the county jail for a term not to exceed six months, or by a fine of not to exceed five hundred dollars ($500), and, if a mineral, oil and gas licensee, he shall be held to trial by the commissioner for a suspension or revocation of his mineral, oil and gas license, as provided in the provisions of this part relating to hearings. It shall be the duty of the district attorney of each county in this State to prosecute all violations of the provisions of this section in respective counties in which the violations occur. -39

Brokers Waiver 10518. In addition to the proof of honesty, truthfulness and good reputation required of an applicant for a mineral, oil and gas license, the commissioner shall ascertain by written examination that the applicant, and in case of a copartnership or corporation applicant for a mineral, oil and gas broker's license that each officer, agent or member thereof through whom it proposes to act as a mineral, oil and gas licensee, has: (a) Appropriate knowledge of the English language, including reading, writing and selling, and of elementary arithmetic. (b) A fair understanding of the general purposes and general legal effect of deeds, mortgages, chattel mortgages, contracts of sale, bills of sale, liens and leases, of the elementary principles of business economics, appraisals, and the purchase, sale, renting and leasing of personal property. (c) A general and fair understanding of the obligations between principal and agent, of the rudiments of geology relating to minerals, oils and gas, and a familiarity with methods of mineral and oil exploration and production, as well as of the provisions of this part relating to mineral, oil and gas brokerage.

Article 3. Bonds 

10540. Every mineral, oil and gas licensee shall file and maintain Bond with the commissioner a bond in the penal sum of five thousand required dollars ($5,000), issued by an admitted, corporate surety insurer, and running to the people of the State of California. The bond shall be conditioned that the licensee will obey all the provisions of this part relating to mineral, oil and gas brokerage, and complete compliance with all obligations assumed by him under his mineral, oll and gas license. In addition to any other remedy he may have, every person sustaining any injury for a breach of obligation may sue the surety for the recovery of any damages sustained by him. The liability of the surety shall not exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000) in the aggregate. -41-

Termination of bond 

Grounds for 10541. The bond shall be continuous in form and remain in full force and effect and shall run concurrently with the license period and for any renewals thereof, as provided in Section 2852 of the Civil Code, unless terminated or cancelled by action of the surety as provided by law or unless terminated or cancelled as provided in this chapter. 

10542. Upon the filing of notice with the commissioner by any surety of its withdrawal as surety for any licensee pursuant to Section 2851 of the Civil Code, the commissioner shall forthwith give notice to the licensee of the withdrawal which notice shall be by registered mail with request for return receipt and shall be addressed to the licensee at his main office as shown by the records of the commissioner. The license of any licensee shall be suspended upon the termination of the bond of the surety as provided in Section 2851 unless, prior to the termination, a new bond has been filed with the commissioner. 

10543. A new bond may be filed at any time by the mineral, oll and gas licensee.

Article 4. Disciplinary Action 

10560. Upon grounds provided in this article and the other articles of this chapter, the license of any mineral, oil and gas licensee may be revoked or suspended in accordance with the provisions of this part relating to hearings. 

10561. The commissioner may, upon his own motion, and shall, disciplinary upon the verified complaint in writing of any person, investigate the action actions of any person engaged in the business or acting in the capacity of a mineral, oil and gas licensee, within this State, and he may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke a mineral, oil and gas license at any time if the licensee, within the immediately preceding three years, while a mineral, oil and gas licensee, in performing or attempting to perform any of the acts within the scope of this chapter, has been guilty of any of the following: Additional grounds 

Report of discharge (a) Making any substantial misrepresentation. (b) Making any false promises of a character likely to influence, persuade or induce. (c) A continued and flagrant course of misrepresentation or making of false promises through mineral, oil and gas brokers or salesmen. (d) Acting for more than one party in a transaction without the knowledge or consent of all parties thereto. (e) Commingling the money or other property of his principal with his own. (f) Any other conduct, whether of the same or a different character than specified in this section, which constitutes fraud or dishonest dealing. 

10562. The commissioner may suspend or revoke the license of any mineral, oil and gas licensee, who within three years immediately preceding has done any of the following: (a) Procured a mineral, oil and gas license, for himself or any salesman, by fraud, misrepresentation or deceit. (b) Been convicted of a felony, knowledge of which the commissioner did not have at the time of last issuing a mineral, oil and gas license to him. (c) Knowingly authorized, directed, connived at or aided in the publication, advertisement, distribution, or circulation of any material false statement or representation concerning his business or any mineral, oil or gas property offered for sale. (d) Wilfully disregarded or violated any of the provisions of this part relating to mineral, oil and gas brokerage. (e) Acted or conducted himself in a manner which would have warranted the denial of his application for a mineral, oil and gas license, or for a renewal thereof. 

10563.
