Section XV Definitions 

AB INITIO-From the beginning. 

AB INITIO MUNDI-From the beginning of the world. 

ABSTRACT-An abridgment; as applied to a record, it means a complete history in short, abbreviated form. 

ABSTRACT OF JUDGMENT-A brief transcript of the essentials of a judgment.

ABSTRACT OF TITLE—A condensed history of the title to land, consisting of a synopsis or summary of the material or operative portion of all the conveyances, of whatever kind or nature, which in any manner affects said land, or any estate or interest therein, together with the statement of all liens, charges, or liabilities, to which the same may be or which it is in any way material for purchases to be apprised. 

ABUTTING OWNERS-Those owners whose lands touch a highway or other public place.

ACCELERATION CLAUSE-A clause in a note, mortgage or deed of trust stipulating that the whole debt shall become due and payable upon the failure of the maker to comply with certain conditions of the contract.

ACCEPTANCE-Act of accepting-approval-agreement to pay. 

The taking and receiving anything in good part, and as it were a tacit agreement to a preceding act, which might have been defeated or avoided if such acceptance had not been made. 

ACCOMMODATION-An obligation assumed without consideration.

ACCRETION-The act of growing to a thing; usually applied to the gradual and imperceptible accumulation of land by natural causes as out of the sea or a river. 

ACKNOWLEDGMENT—The act by which a party has executed an instrument of conveyance as grantor goes before a competent officer or court and declares or acknowledges the same as his genuine and voluntary act and deed.

The certificate of the officer on such instrument that it has been so acknowledged. 

ACQUISITION-The act of process by which a person procures property. The process of acquisition by an act or law in the cases of forfeiture, succession, marriage, judgment, insolvency, or by the act of the parties as by gift or sale. 

ACT-ACTS-In its general legal sense this noun denotes something done by an individual, as a private citizen, or as an officer; or by a body of men, as a legislature, a council, or a court of justice; including not merely physical acts, but also decrees, edicts, laws, judgments, resolves, awards and determinations. 

An instrument in writing to verify facts. -356-

ACT OF GOD-An irresistible disaster, the result of natural causes, such as earthquakes, violent storms, lightning, unprecedented floods.

ACTION FOR SEPARATE MAINTENANCE-An action by a mar ried woman who is compelled through her husband's fault to live apart from him, by which action she is allowed separate maintenance or permanent alimony without divorce. 

ACTION IN PERSONAM-An action which has for its object a judgment against the person as distinguished from a judgment against property to determine its status. (Example: an action for services rendered.)

ACTION IN REM-An action which has for its object a judgment against property to determine its status. (Example: an action to foreclose a mortgage.)

ACTION TO QUIET TITLE-An action to effect the removal of a cloud or clouds on title to property. 

AD-At; to; before; near; for; of; until; within. 

AD CURIAM-Before the court; to the court. 

AD ITEM-During the pendency of the action or proceeding. 

AD TERMINUM ANNORUM-For a term of years. 

AD VALOREM-According to the value-from the value. 

When the duty or tax is laid in the form of a percentage on the value of the property. 

ADJUST-To bring to proper relations; to settle; to determine and apportion an amount due. 

ADMINISTRATOR-One appointed by a proper court to administer the estate of a deceased person. The same as an executor except that an executor is appointed by the deceased and bond is not necessarily required, whereas an administrator is required by the court to furnish administration bond. 

ADMINISTRATOR C. T. A.-Abbreviation for administrator cum testamento annexo.

ADMINISTRATOR CUM TESTAMENTO ANNEXO-An adminis trator with the will annexed, that is, an administrator of a decedent whose will named no executor or named an executor who cannot or will not act.

ADMINISTRATOR D. B. N.-Abbreviation for administrator de bonis non-"de bonis non" meaning: of goods or property upon which no administration has been had. 

ADMINISTRATOR DE BONIS NON: See above. 

ADVERSE POSSESSION-Actual holding and enjoyment of land under a claim of right which is opposed to or inconsistent with another's claims. 

AFFIANT—A person who has made an affidavit. 

AFFIDAVIT-A sworn statement in writing before a proper official.

AFFIRM-To confirm, to aver, to ratify, to verify. -357-

AGENCY-The relation between a principal and his agent-business of one entrusted with the concerns of another. 

AGENDA-Things to be done; matters to be attended to. 

AGREEMENT OF SALE-An instrument in writing that implies an obligation to sell, but may also imply an obligation on the part of the other party to buy. 

AGRICULTURAL LAND-Generally speaking agricultural land is that land adaptable and subject to use for agricultural purposes. 

Land may be assessable as "agricultural land" though it be covered by native timber and underbrush, grass or weeds. 

ALCALDE-Chief magistrate or mayor. (Spanish). 

ALLAS "Otherwise called"-another name; assumed.

ALIEN-A foreigner; a person residing in one country, but owing allegiance to another.

ALIENATION-Conveyance or transfer of property; estrange; 

separate from.

ALIMONY—An allowance to either spouse upon a decree of divorce or pending the suit (pendente lite).

ALITER Otherwise. 

ALLEGATION-An assertion; a statement of fact in a pleading. 

ALLUVION-Deposits of earth or other material made by natural action of water.

ALLUVIUM-Matter derived from natural waste of rocks, carried away by running water and gradually deposited in some other place, there forming a deposit for new soil. 

AMORTIZATION-The operation of paying off bonds, stock, a mortgage, trust deed, or other indebtedness by installments, or by a sinking fund.

ANCILLARY-Auxiliary. 

ANNUITY-A sum paid yearly or at stated intervals. 

ANNUL-To cancel; make void; destroy. To abrogate, nullify or abolish. ANTE-Before.

ANTENUPTIAL-Before marriage. 

APPEARANCE-The coming into court of a party to a suit.

APPRAISE-APPRAISING-To fix or set a price or value upon; 

to fix and state the true value of a thing, usually, in writing.

APPURTENANCE-Equipment, improvements or other rights which go with the land, although not covered by description; an adjunct; an appendage; something annexed to another thing more worthy as principal and which passes as incident to it. 

A PRIORI-From the past; from what has previously transpired. 

ASSESSED VALUATION—The estimated worth or value of personal or real property determined by the county assessor, or a related agency, such as the board of equalization, and upon the determined worth of the property the assessment is levied. (One -358-

should not be misled in judging the real value of property by the assessed valuation.)

ASSESSMENTS-As distinguished from other kinds of taxation, assessments are those special and local impositions upon property, in the immediate vicinity of municipal improvements, which are necessary to pay for the special benefit which the property is supposed to have derived therefrom. 

Assessment and tax are not synonymous although occasionally so used.

ASSIGNEE-One to whom an assignment has been made. 

ASSIGNER-One who assigns.

ASSIGNMENT-The writing by which an interest is transferred. 

ASSIGNOR-One who makes an assignment or transfers property to another; an assigner. 

ASSIGNS-A special use of "assignees," used in legal instruments as "his heirs and assigns.' 

ASSUMING MORTGAGE-By "assuming a mortgage" is meant an act or agreement of taking upon oneself a debt or obligation primarily resting upon another, i. e., adoption of the mortgage debt and becoming personally liable for its payment, irrespective of the market price of the property hypothecated as security for the mortgage.

ASSUMPSIT-An undertaking, express or implied, to do some act or make some payment.

ATTACHMENT-An act or process of seizing personal or real property by virtue of judicial order to bring the same into the custody of the law as security for a debt or cost. 

ATTESTATION CLAUSE-That clause in a deed denoting that the persons signing are witnesses.

ATTORN-To accept and acknowledge a new landlord; to appoint an attorney or substitute.

ATTORNEY-IN-FACT—One authorized to act for another by a writing designated as "power of attorney."

AUTHORIZATION TO SELL-A written instrument by which one authorizes another to sell their property. 

AVULSION-The removal of a considerable quantity of soil from the land of one man, and its deposit upon or annexation to the land of another, suddenly and by the perceptible action of water. 

AYUNTAMIENTO-Town council. (Spanish). 

BASE AND MERIDIAN-Imaginary geographical lines used for designating, locating and describing subdivisions of public or private lands. In California lands are described as Township number.... North or South of Base line, and Range number.... 

East or West of Meridian line; Humboldt Peak Base and 

Meridian in the Northern, Mount Diablo Base and Meridian in the Central, San Bernardino Base and Meridian in the Southern part of the state. 

BENEFICIARY-One for whose benefit a trust is created. The person to whom a policy of insurance is payable. -359-

BENEVOLENT ASSOCIATIONS-Voluntary aggregations of in dividuals or bodies corporate formed, not for profit, but to render financial aid or other assistance to members. 

BEQUEATH-To give or leave by will. 

BEQUEST That which is left by will. 

BETTERMENTS Substantial improvements upon an estate. 

B. F.-Abbreviation of "bonum factum," meaning good deed. 

A valid decree. 

BID-An offer (noun).

BILL OF EXCHANGE-A written order from one person to an other, ordering him to pay a third person. Drafts; acceptances.

BILL OF SALE-A written instrument evidencing the transfer of personal property.

BILLS PAYABLE-Notes or acceptances issued. Obligations due another liabilities.

BILLS RECEIVABLE-Notes or acceptances taken. Money due assets.

BLUE SKY LAWS-Statutes regulating investment companies, the conduct of their business and the issuance and sale of their securities.

BONA-Goods; chattels. 

BONA FIDE-In or with good faith; honestly, sincerely, openly; without deceit or fraud.

BONAE FIDEI EMPTOR-A purchaser in good faith. 

BOND-A contract by specialty to pay a certain sum of money; being an instrument under seal, by which the maker or obligor promises and binds himself, his heirs, executors, and administrators to pay a designated sum of money to another upon the failure of performance of certain conditions, usually to be performed by a third party.

Used as negotiable paper denoting debentures or evidences of indebtedness.

BONDED DEBT-An indebtedness secured by a bond issue. 

BOUNDS-Boundaries. 

BREACH-The violation of an obligation.

BROKER(Real Estate.) See Section 2-California Real Estate Law. 

BUILDING LINE-Lines established by ordinance or statute be tween which and the street the property owner may not build. 

BY-LAW-A rule of a corporation for its government. 

CAMINO-A highway. (Spanish). 

CAPITA-Heads; persons. 

CAPITATION TAXES 

Poll taxes.

CAPTION-The heading or title of a document. 

CAUSE-An action or suit. 

-360-

CAVEAT-Let him beware.

A formal warning against the per formance of certain acts. 

CAVEAT EMPTOR-Let the buyer beware, i. e., He must examine goods and make purchase at his own peril as to patent defects. CESTUI-He.

CESTUI QUE TRUST-The person for whose benefit property is held in trust by a trustee.

CESTUI QUE USE-The person for whose use land was granted to another.

CESTUI QUE VIE-The person for the duration of whose lifetime an estate has been granted.

CHANGE OF VENUE-The removal of a cause for trial from one county to another.

CHATTEL INTEREST-All interest in personal property. 

CHATTEL MORTGAGE-A mortgage on personal property, as dis tinguished from one on real property.

CHATTELS-Articles of personal property-things personal and movable.

CHOSE IN ACTION—A thing in action, that is, a thing of which the owner has not possession but only a right to bring an action for its possession or for damages. 

CIRCA-About; around; concerning.

CLIENT-A person who employs or retains another to act for him or to perform certain specified services.

CLOUD ON TITLE-An outstanding claim or encumbrance which, if valid, would affect or impair the title of the owner.

CODE-A system of law. 

COLLATERAL-Subordinate; indirect; as, collateral causes, security attached to another to secure performance; additional obligation or security; as, a collateral loan.

COLLATERAL SECURITY-A secondary security to be available if the chief security fails.

COLLECTIVE-Gathered into one mass, sum or body; united, as collective revenues; collective actions. 

COLLUSION-Deceit; secret agreement, or cooperation for fraud.

COLOR OF TITLE-Apparent title; a prima facie title which is in reality invalid.

COMMERCIAL ACRE-A term in use by real estate subdividers as descriptive of a parcel of land comprising a remainder of an acre after proportionate deductions therefrom have been made for use of streets and alleys in a subdivision.

COMMERCIAL PAPER-Bills of exchange, or notes given in course of trade.

COMMISSIONS-A term used to designate conditional earnings, on a percentage basis, for services rendered. -361-

COMMON LAW-(a) The body of customs, usages and practices developed and administered by the Anglo-Saxons. The body of 

English Law as distinguished from Roman Law, canon law, and other systems. (b) The ancient unwritten law founded on immemorial customs and precedents as distinguished from statute law.

COMMUNIS PARIES-A party wall. 

COMMUNITY PROPERTY-Property owned in common by hus band and wife-property acquired by husband and wife, or either, during marriage, when not acquired as the separate property of either.

COMPETENT-Duly qualified; able; adequate; sufficient; capable; legally and mentally fit. 

COMPLETION-The finishing or accomplishing in full of something theretofore begun; substantial performance of what one has agreed to do; state in which no essential element is lacking. 

COMPOSITION—An agreement between a debtor and his creditors whereby the latter mutually agree to accept a certain percentage less than is due each one. 

CONDEMNATION-The exercise of the power of eminent domain. 

CONDITIONAL SALE CONTRACT-A contract for the sale of personal or real property which is dependent upon, or granted subject to, a condition or conditions. Usually provides that property sold shall be paid for in installments, the seller retaining title thereto. Also usually contains a clause providing for cancellation of contract and forfeiture of any money paid, as rental, in event of default in one or more payments. 

CONFESS JUDGMENT-To submit voluntarily to the action of the court without process.

CONGRESSIONAL GRANT-A grant of public land of the United 

States made by an act of Congress.

CONSIDERATION-The inducement to a contract. The cause, motive, price, or impelling influence which induces a party to enter into a contract.

CONSTRUCTIVE NOTICE-Notice given by the public records. "Constructive Notice"-is a presumption of law, making it impossible for one to deny the matter concerning which notice is given. The occupation of property in actual, open possession would tend to the presumption that such occupant had an interest in such property and would be construed as "constructive notice."

CONTIGUOUS-In actual or close contact; touching; adjacent; near.

CONTRACT-An agreement to do or not to do certain things. 

CONTRACTOR-One who enters into a contract to do or not to do certain things. -362-

CONVEYANCE-As generally used it denotes any transfer of title legal or equitable. An instrument in writing under seal by which some estate or interest in lands is transferred from one person to another; such as a deed, mortgage, etc. 

CORPORAL-Affecting or relating to the body. 

CORPORATION-An artificial being created by law and endowed with certain of the rights, privileges and duties of natural persons.

CORPORATION SOLE-A corporation consisting of a single person, and his successor, incorporated by law to give such person certain advantages, particularly that of perpetuity, which otherwise he could not have had. 

CORPOREAL-Having a body; tangible. 

CORPOREAL HEREDITAMENTS-Such inheritable property as may be perceived by the senses.

COURT OF EQUITY-One having a chancery or equity jurisdic tion. See equity.

COVENANT-A particular agreement or stipulation contained in a deed or other document incidental to its main purpose. 

CROFT-A small farm. 

C. T. A.-An abbreviation of cum testamento annexo. (With will annexed.) See Administrator C. T. A.

CURTESY-The life estate or the tenure which (in some states, but not in California) the husband has in the lands of his deceased wife, which by the common law takes effect where he has had issue by her, born alive, and capable of inheriting the lands. 

CUSTOMER-One with whom you do business but by whom you are not employed.

DAMAGES The indemnity recoverable by a person who has sustained an injury, either in his person, property, or relative rights, through the act or default of another. d. b. n.-An abbreviation of de bonis non. 

D. B. N.) dd.-An abbreviation of "days after date." 

De-From; of; concerning. (See Administrator

DEED-A written instrument, signed, sealed and delivered by the terms of which one person conveys land, tenements, or hereditaments to another.

De Facto-In fact. 

DEFAULT-The omission or failure to fulfill a duty, observe a promise; discharge an obligation or perform an agreement. 

DEFEASANCE CLAUSE-A clause in mortgage which states that upon fulfillment of conditions, security is to be reconveyed to mortgagee.

DEFICIENCY JUDGMENT-A personal judgment against any person liable for the mortgage or trust deed debt for the amount remaining due the mortgagee or beneficiary after foreclosure. -363-

DEFUNCT-Dead. 

DE JURE-By right. 

DEMISE-A transfer, a lease, a transfer to another of an estate for years, for life or at will.

DEPONENT-A witness; an affiant. 

DEPRECIATION-The deterioration, or the loss or lessening in the value arising from age, use, and improvements, due to better methods. A fall in value. Reduction of worth. 

DERAIGN—To trace; to prove.

DESCENT-Hereditary succession. 

DEVISE-A gift of real property by will. 

DEVISEE-Party to whom testator leaves an estate in real property.

DICTA-Plural of dictum. 

DICTUM-An opinion by a judge on a point not essential to the decision on the main question. 

DIES-A day.

DILUVION-The gradual washing away and consequent loss of soil along the banks of a river. 

DIRECTIONAL GROWTH-A term used in real estate to indicate the direction in which a community seems to be developing. 

DISSEISIN-Ouster. 

DIVISA-A boundary. 

DIVEST-To deprive of a right or title. 

DONA-Gifts. 

DONEE A person to whom a gift is made. 

DONOR-A person who makes a gift. 

DOWER-The legal right or interest which the wife acquires (in some states, but not in California) by marriage in the real estate of her husband.

DRY FARMING This term is used to indicate farming done without irrigation.

DURESS-Imprisonment used for illegal purpose; threats of bodily harm, or other means amounting to or tending to coerce the will of another, or actually inducing him to do an act contrary to his free will.

EARNEST Something given as a part of the purchase price to bind a bargain.

EASEMENT-Any of several rights which one person may have in the land of another.

ECONOMIC GOODS-Possessions real or personal which are the equivalent of, or constitute wealth.

ELEEMOSYNARY-Charitable. 

ELISOR-A person appointed to perform certain duties pertaining to certain officers (especially sheriff or coroner) when the latter are disqualified. -364-

EMINENT DOMAIN-The supreme right in the government to take private property for public use. 

EMPTOR-A buyer. 

ENFEOFF To vest a person with the fee. 

EQUITABLE TITLE The right in the party to whom it belongs to have the legal title transferred to him. 

EQUITY-State or quality of being equal or fair; fairness; equitable; fair; just; reasonable.

EQUITY OF REDEMPTION-The right which the mortgagor of an estate has of redeeming it, after it has been forfeited at law by the non-payment of the money it was given to secure. 

EQUIVALENT-Equal in worth; effect; meaning. 

EROSION-The gradual eating away of the soil by the operation of currents or tides. Distinguished from submergence, which is the disappearance of the soil under the water and the formation of a navigable body over it.

ESCHEAT-The lapsing or reverting of land to the state for failure of heirs, or for illegal ownership. 

ESCROW-A deposit of an instrument with a third party to be delivered to the other party upon the fulfillment of certain conditions.

ESTATE-A person's fortune; possessions, which may be either real or personal property.

ESTATE AT WILL The occupation of lands and tenements by a tenant for an indefinite period; may be for specified terms, etc. 

A form of lease. 

ESTATE FOR LIFE-A freehold estate, not of inheritance, but which is held by the tenant for his own life or for an indefinite period which may endure for the life or lives of persons in being, and not beyond the period of a life. 

ESTATE FOR YEARS-An interest in lands by virtue of a contract for the possession of them for a definite and limited period of time. A lease may be said to be an estate for years. 

ESTATE IN SEVERALTY-An estate held by a person in his own right only without any other person being joined or connected with him in point of interest. This is the most common and usual way of holding an estate. 

ESTATE OF INHERITANCE-An estate which may descend to heirs. All freehold estates are estates of inheritance, except estates for life.

ESTOPPEL-A bar which precludes a person, in law, from asserting rights in contravention of his previous position or representations.

ETHICS That branch of moral science, idealism, justness, and fairness, which treats of the duties which a member of a profession or craft, owes to the public, to his clients or patron, and to his professional brethren or members. -365-

EXCHANGE AGREEMENT—An instrument by which two or more people agree to exchange property subject to conditions written into the agreement. When signed by all parties having an interest in the properties being exchanged, within the time limit expressed, it is binding on the parties thereto. 

EXCLUSIVE AGENCY OR EXCLUSIVE LISTING-An instru ment whereby an owner grants to a broker the right to sell certain property for a specific period of time to the exclusion of anyone else other than the owner.

EXCLUSIVE RIGHT-A term contained in a lasting contract which entitles the listing broker to full commission if property is sold within the time limit by himself, any other broker or the owner. 

EXECUTE-To complete, to follow through to the end. To perform what is required to give validity to, as by signing, sealing and delivering a deed.

EXECUTER-One who executes. 

EXECUTOR-An executer; one named in a person's will as the one to execute it, or see that its provisions are carried out. 

EXECUTRIX-A woman executor. 

EXPEDIENTE-A complete statement of every step taken in the proceedings to acquire a Mexican grant.

EX POST FACTO-After the event. 

EXPRESS-Definite; clear.

FACSIMILE-An exact and precise copy. 

FACTA-Facts; deeds; act.

FACTOR-An agent employed to transact business for another. 

FEE-An unlimited estate of inheritance; the highest estate which there is in land. Also used instead of commission, as a broker's fee.

FEE SIMPLE-An absolute fee; a fee without limitation to any 

FEE SIMPLE ESTATE-One in which the owner is entitled to the entire property with unconditional power of disposing of it during his life and it may descend to his heirs and legal representatives upon his death without his having made a will. particular class of heirs or restrictions. 

FEME COVERT-A married woman. 

FEME SOLE-An unmarried woman. 

FIDUCIARY-One who holds property in trust for another; a trustee.

FORECLOSURE OF MORTGAGE-A process in chancery by which all further right existing in a mortgagor to redeem an estate is defeated and lost to him and the estate becomes the absolute property of the mortgagee. This term is also applicable when the mortgagor has forfeited his estate by non-payment of the money due on the mortgage at the time appointed, but still retains the equity of redemption. Under California law the mortgagor retains equity of redemption for one year after foreclosure. -366

"FORECLOSURE" OF TRUST DEED-Strictly speaking there is no such thing as a "foreclosure" of a trust deed. Upon default by the trustor the beneficiary may prepare a "Declaration of Default" and "Request for Sale." The trustee has these recorded. Twenty days or more before date set for sale a notice of time and place of sale must be mailed to each person having an interest therein. Under a Trust Deed the beneficiary may secure title in about 110 days, and there is no equity of redemption.

FRANCHISE—A special privilege or particular right conferred and granted by competent authority, and vested in individuals or corporations. 

FRAUD-An intentional perversion of truth (whether by words or conduct, by false or misleading allegations or by concealment of that which should have been disclosed), resulting in loss of property or surrender of a legal right. 

FREEHOLD-An estate in land or other real property of uncertain duration; that is, either of inheritance or which may possibly last for the life of the tenant at the least, (as distinguished from a leasehold); and held by a free tenure. An estate to be a freehold must be "real estate" and must be of indeterminate duration.

FUNDED Made into a permanent loan on which interest is paid, as "funded debt."

GARNISH-To cause a garnishment to be levied on a person. 

GARNISHEE-The serving of a writ of garnishment on a person ordering him to appear in court, and give information in regard to the goods of another in his possession. 

GARNISHMENT-A proceeding whereby property, money or credits of a debtor in possession of another (the garnishee) are applied to the payment of the debts by means of process against the debtor and garnishee.

GORE-A small, triangular piece of land. 

GRANT-A transfer of property, real or personal, by deed or writing. In personal property "grant" is often used as an equivalent to assignment as distinguished from a gift. 

GRANTEE The person to whom a grant or conveyance is made. 

GRANTOR The person who makes a grant or conveyance. 

GROIN-Any structure offering or intended to offer substantial resistance to the coastwise movement of littoral sands. 

GUARDIAN-A person to whom the law has instructed the custody and control of the person or estate, or both, of a minor or incompetent person.

HABENDUM-That part of a deed the purpose of which is to repeat the name of the grantee, to describe the estate conveyed and to what use.

HABENDUM ET TENENDUM-To have and to hold. 

HAND-A lineal measure of four inches. -367-

HEIRS-Those persons appointed by law to succeed to the real estate of a decedent in case he left no will. In a broader sense, the term indicates those who come in any manner to the ownership of any property by reason of the death of an owner. 

HEREDITAMENTS-Things which may be inherited. 

HOLDER IN DUE COURSE-A person who has received a check or note in due course of business, before it was overdue, and without notice that it had been previously dishonored and who took the check or note in good faith and for value, and that at the time it was negotiated to him he had no notice of any defect in the title of the person who negotiated it. Under California 

Law such "holder in due course" may collect face value of such note or check from the person who originally issued same even though it is later proven that such note or check was obtained from the person who issued same by fraud or theft. 

HOLOGRAPHIC WILL-A will entirely written, dated and signed by the testator in his own handwriting.

HOMESTEAD-The homestead consists of the dwelling house in which the claimant resides, and the land on which the same is situated, selected in the manner provided by law. The head of a household may declare a homestead in the amount of $5,000; a single person in the amount of $1,000. 

HYPOTHECATE-To pledge as security while still retaining pos session.

IDEM SONANS-The doctrine that if two names may be sounded alike any variance in spelling is immaterial and the names are idem sonans. 

ID EST That is; that is to say. i. e. An abbreviation of id est. 

INCOMPETENT-Lack of ability, legal qualifications or fitness to discharge the required duty-a person who is unfit to manage his own affairs by reason of insanity, imbecility, or feeble-mindedness. Minors, i. e., persons under the age of 21 years. Women over 18 when married are of legal age to convey property. 

INCUMBRANCE-Anything amounting to a claim, limitation, or restriction on property. An incumbrance does not necessarily lower the value of property but in some cases definitely enhances the value.

INDORSEMENT-The writing of one's name on the back of a bill, note, check or other negotiable instrument, constitutes an indorsement of such instrument and unless qualified with the words "without recourse" over such signature, constitutes a guarantee of payment of the face value of such instrument. 

IN ESSE-In being; alive.

INJUNCTION—A writ or order issued under the seal of a court to restrain one or more parties to a suit or proceeding from doing or permitting others who are under his control to do an act which is deemed to be inequitable or unjust in regard to the rights of some other party or parties in the suit or proceeding. -368-

IN PERSONAM—Against the person. 

IN PROPRIA PERSONA-In his own person; himself; as, the defendant appears in propria persona. IN RE-In the matter of. 

IN REM-Against a thing and not against a person.

INSTALLMENT NOTE-A note providing for the partial payment thereof in installments at periodic intervals as provided in the instrument. 

INSTRUMENT-A document or writing which gives formal expression to a legal act of agreement for the purpose of creating, securing, modifying or terminating a right. 

INTER ALIA-Among other things. 

INTERLOCUTORY-Provisional; temporary; not final. 

INTESTATE-Without a will; a person who has died without a will.

INTRA-Within. 

IPSO FACTO-Of itself; by that very fact.

IRREVOCABLE-Incapable of being recalled or revoked; unchangeable; unalterable. 

JOINDER-Acting jointly with one or more persons; joining.

JOINT TENANCY-Joint or equal ownership of property automatically carrying "right of survivorship." Vests entire title in surviving tenant without probate. 

JUDGMENT-The final determination, decision, decree or sentence of a court.

JUDGMENT-PROOF-A term to denote that an individual, partnership or corporation has no tangible assets by virtue of which a creditor may force collection by attachment or execution. 

JURAT-A certificate evidencing the fact that an affidavit was properly made before a duly authorized officer. 

JURISDICTION-The right to adjudicate concerning the subject matter in a given case.

KEY LOT-A term used to designate a lot or business site which faces at right angles to and abuts the rear of lots facing on another street. A key lot is considered less desirable than other lots in the same tract. 

LACHES-Inexcusable delay in asserting a right.

LAND CONTRACT-A contract for the sale of real property be tween the seller or trustee and the buyer whereby property is sold on an installment payment plan, the seller holding legal title until all the terms of the contract have been complied with. 

LANDS, TENEMENTS AND HEREDITAMENTS-A phrase used in the early English law to express all sorts of property of the immovable class. Its present use may be said to express real estate with all fixed improvements thereon, if any. 

LATENT-Concealed. 

-369

LATERAL-Pertaining to, proceeding from, or directed toward the side.

LEASE Contract whereby possession of land or buildings, etc., is granted by owner for a specified term of months or years, usually subject to payment of rent. 

A lease for one year or less may be oral; for more than one year it must be in writing. 

LEGATEE-Party to whom testator leaves any property, real or personal.

LESSEE One to whom a lease is given or who takes an estate by lease; a tenant under a lease. 

LESSOR-One who leases or gives a lease. 

LIEN-The right to legally hold and control property of another until a debt is paid or legal claim discharged-generally evidenced by trust deeds or mortgages where lien is voluntary. 

Such liens are specific. 

LINEAL-In a direct line. 

LIQUID ASSETS-A state of being liquid-readily convertible into cash.

LIQUIDATE—To pay, settle a debt-to wind up affairs of a business and apportion assets and debts; conversion of property and other assets into cash.

LIS PENDENS-Suit pending-generally used to define the state of suit where complaint has been filed and notice of pending court action.

LISTINGS-A written authorization given by the owner to the broker to sell the owner's property.

LITE PENDENTE-While the action is pending. 

LITTORAL-Pertaining to the shore. 

MARKETABLE TITLE "A marketable title" to land is such a title as a court of equity, when asked to decree specific performance of a contract of sale, will compel the vendee to accept as sufficient a title free from plausible or reasonable objections.

MARKET PRICE-The actual price at which the given commodity is currently sold, or has recently been sold, in the open marketin usual and ordinary course of trade and competition, between seller and buyer equally free to bargain, as established by records of late sales.

MARKET VALUE-The price which an article or piece of prop erty might be expected to bring if offered for sale in a fair market; not the price which might be obtained on a sale at public auction or a sale forced by the necessities of the owner, but such a price as would be fixed by negotiation and mutual agreements after ample time and advertising to find a purchaser. -370-

MATTOON ACT-The Acquisition and Improvement Act of 1925, repealed August 21, 1933. This improvement act differs from others in that assessments were levied against entire districts divided into zones rather than against particular parcels of land, and collected with taxes. Under this Act the owners of property in the zone were responsible and subject to taxation on the` whole district or zone individually and collectively. MEAN-Intermediate. 

MEANDER-To follow a winding course.

MECHANICS' LIEN-A type of lien created by statute in favor of persons who have performed work or furnished material in or for the erection of a building. This lien attaches to the land as well as the building and is a priority claim when executed and filed as provided by law. 

MEMORIAL-A short note, abstract or memorandum. 

MESNE Intermediate; intervening; mean.

METES AND BOUNDS-Description used in conveyancing (generally where there is no recorded map) the boundary line on lands, with their terminating points and angles. 

MINORS-One who is under the age of legal competence, i. e., persons under the age of 21 years. In California, women over 18 when married are of legal age to convey property or execute any contract if otherwise qualified.

MORATORIUM-A right given by law to delay discharge of monetary obligations for a certain period, sometimes legally authorized during times of financial distress. 

MORTGAGE-An instrument used for the hypothecation of property as security for the payment of a debt or the performance of an obligation. It is a specific, not a general, lien. 

MORTGAGEE-The person to whom property is mortgaged. He who takes or receives a mortgage. 

MORTGAGOR-The owner who gives a mortgage as security for the payment or performance of an obligation. 

MUNIMENTS OF TITLE-Title deeds and other original docu ments showing a chain of title.

NATURALIZATION—The grant of citizenship to an alien by the nation.

NATURALIZED CITIZEN-A person who has been made a citizen of the United States under an act of Congress. 

NEAP TIDES-Those tides which happen between the full and change of the moon, twice in every twenty-four hours.

NEGOTIABLE-Capable of being negotiated; assignable or transferable in the ordinary course of business. 

NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS-A general name for bills, notes, checks, drafts or other written obligations, which are subject to transfer by endorsement and delivery or by delivery merely, so as to vest in the endorsee the legal title. -371-

NET LISTINGS-Listings where commission equals excess of sale above net price. The net price the owner expects to receive after payment of commission to selling broker. 

NON SEQUITUR-It does not follow. 

NONSUIT-A judgment given against the plaintiff when he is unable to prove a case or when he refuses or neglects to proceed to the trial after it has been put at issue without determining such issue.

NOTARY PUBLIC-A public officer whose function is to administer oaths; to attest and certify, by his hand and official seal, certain classes of documents, to give them authenticity; and to perform certain other official acts chiefly in commercial matters such as the protesting of notes and bills, etc. 

NOTES-Negotiable instruments evidencing an obligation—an ab stract, a memorandum; an informal statement in writing. 

NOTICE Information. An advice, or written warning intended to apprise a person or persons of some proceeding in which his or their interests are involved. 

NOVATION-The substitution of a new obligation in place of an existing one.

NULLA BONA RETURN-The return of the sheriff or other officer on execution unsatisfied. (Nulla bona means "no goods".) 

NUNC PRO TUNC-Now for then. A tardy act made retroactive so as to take effect as of the time when it should have been done.

NUNCUPATIVE WILL-A will declared orally and not in writing. 

OBITER DICTA-Plural of obiter dictum. 

OBITER DICTUM-That which is said in passing.

OBSOLESCENCE-The condition or process of gradually falling into disuse.

OFFSET STATEMENT-An owner's statement (in effect an abstract) usually made when hypothecating property; a statement showing the condition of a note, etc.

OMNIBUS CLAUSE-That clause in a decree of distribution by which "any other property not now known or discovered which may belong to said estate or in which said estate may have any interest" passes to the distributees named without specific description.

OPEN LISTING Signed listing by owner authorizing broker to sell property at price and at terms specified. Does not protect broker for Commissions against sales made by owner or other brokers. 

OPERATIVE PROPERTY-Any property which may be reason ably necessary for use in the operation and conduct of the particular kind or kinds of business in which such property is employed. -372-

OPTION-A privilege existing in a person or persons called the "optionee" for which a consideration has been given, which the owner (optionor) grants to the holder the right to buy certain merchandise or property, if he chooses, at any time within an agreed period at a fixed price, or to sell such property to another person or persons at an agreed price within the specified period. 

OPTIONEE—One who buys or receives an option giving him the exclusive right within a given time, to do certain things, but without binding him to do those things. 

OPTIONOR-One who evidences by an instrument called an "option" that he has granted to another party the privilege or right, for a period of time, to do certain things (such as the right to buy the property specified in the option at the price specified.) 

This is binding on the optionor but is not binding on the optionee. 

ORAL-Verbal; spoken.

ORAL AUTHORIZATION-VERBAL-In the sale or leasing of real estate the courts have ruled that payment of commission can not be forced unless agreement is in writing. 

ORIGINAL CONTRACTOR-One who, for a fixed price, agrees with owner to perform certain work and/or supply certain material.

OVERT-Open. 

OWNERSHIP-The complete dominion, title, or proprietary right in a thing or claim. The right of one or more persons to possess and use, or dispose of, a thing to the exclusion of others. 

PARI PASSU-In equal degree; pro rata. 

PAROL-Oral. 

PARTIAL RELEASE CLAUSE-A clause in a trust deed or mort gage which provides for the release from such trust deed or mortgage of a specified part of the property held as security. 

Generally provides that such release shall be made upon the payment of a sum in excess of the proportionate share which would ordinarily apply to the part released. Mostly used in connection with financing subdivisions.

PARTNERSHIP-The association of two or more persons for the purpose of carrying on business together and dividing the profits between them.

PARTY IN POSSESSION-Indicates that such party has some rights in the property in which they have possession. Possession of property is notice that should be considered by any prospective lienor or purchaser before such party makes a loan or purchases property. Some contracts evidencing equitable title to property are not necessarily recorded and might give party in possession a prior lien (land contracts, etc.).

PARTY WALL-A wall for the common benefit and use of two owners, their property being separated by the wall. -373-

PAR VALUE-The face value. 

PATENT-A conveyance of title to government land by the government.

PAYEE-The person in whose favor a bill of exchange, promissory note, or check is made or drawn. 

PAYOR-One who pays, or who is to make a payment. 

PENALTY—A punishment imposed by statute as a consequence of the commission of an offense. 

PENDENTE LITE-Pending suit. 

PER AUTRE VIE-During the life of another. 

PER CAPITA-By the head, that is, by the number of individuals. 

PER SE-By itself; as such. 

PERSONAL PROPERTY—All property that is not real property movable property-property that is not land or those things permanently attached to land. 

PLEDGE-A pawn; a bailment of personal property as security for some debt or engagement.

POLICE POWER-The power vested in a state to establish laws and ordinances for the regulation and enforcement of its policethe power vested in the legislature to make, ordain, and establish laws, statutes, and ordinances, either with penalties or without, not repugnant to the Constitution, as they shall judge to be for the good and welfare of the commonwealth, and the majority of its citizens.

POSSESSION-The detention and control of anything which may be the subject of property, for one's use and enjoyment, either as owner or as the proprietor of a qualified right in it, and either held personally or by another who exercises it in one's place and name.

POSSESSIONS-All things of which one has possession, or some right or title to.

POST-After-subsequent to-following. 

POWER OF ATTORNEY-Written authority from one person to another to act for him.

PREAMBLE-An introductory part. 

PRE-EMPTION-The act of buying anything before or ahead of another person.

PRE-EMPTION ENTRY-An entry by a settler upon public lands of the United States. Where such entry is made the entryman secures a preferred right to acquire the land by virtue of his occupation and improvement. 

PRESCRIPTION-Title obtained in law by long possession. Occu pancy for the period prescribed by the Code of Civil Procedure as sufficient to bar an action for the recovery of the property gives title by prescription. 

PRIMA FACIE-On its face; presumptively.

PRINCIPAL One who employs another to act for him. -374-

PRIVITY-Closeness or mutuality or relationship, as privity of interests.

PROPERTY-That which belongs exclusively to one-an aggregate of rights which are guaranteed and protected by the government; ownership; the unrestricted and exclusive right to a thing; the right to dispose of a thing in every legal way, to possess it, to use it, and to exclude everyone else from interfering with it. 

PROPERTY MANAGEMENT-The managing, renting, supervising repairs and general handling of the property tending to the best interests of the owner.

PRORATION OF TAXES-To divide, share, or distribute propor tionally.

PRO TANTO-For so much; to that extent. 

PURCHASE-Buying for a sum of money-acquiring property other than by inheritance or gift.

PURCHASE MONEY (mortgage or trust deed)-A sum given for all or part of the purchase price of real property at the time of its conveyance-differs from borrowed money. Secured by mortgage or trust deed in that it represents a specific lien and is not subject to deficiency judgment. 

QUASI-As if; analagous; of a similar nature.

QUIT CLAIM DEED-Deed by which grantor relinquishes all interest he may have in a property. q. v.: (Quod vide.)-Which see.

RACE RESTRICTIONS-Restriction against the use or occupancy by persons other than of the Caucasian race. Restrictions against the sale to such persons is not enforceable as it is restraint on alienation or conveyance of title. 

RANGE-A term to denote one of the divisions of a state, and designates a row or tier of townships as they appear on the map; used in the description or designation of property. 

RATABLE-Taxable. 

REALTY BOARDS-Private organizations having no official status, organized for the purpose of forwarding the interests of brokers, disseminating education, and raising the standards of real estate practice. 

REAL PROPERTY-Immovable property-the earth, anything permanently attached thereto, or buried beneath it.

REALTOR-One who is a member of a realty board. 

RECONVEYANCE-A transfer of title to land back to a former owner, as an estate. In California used particularly in denoting the transferring of the legal title by the trustee to the trustor under a trust deed.

REDDENDUM-The clause in a conveyance reserving the rent to the grantor; also a clause in a deed by which some new thing is reserved out of what had been granted before. -375-

REDEMPTION—The act of redeeming property conditionally lost through foreclosure of mortgage or sale by trustee within the time specified by law.

REDEMPTIONER-One who redeems. 

RELEASE-The relinquishment, concession, or giving up of a right, claim, or privilege by the person in whom it exists or to whom it accrues, to the person against whom it might have been demanded or enforced.

RELEASE CLAUSE-This is a stipulation that upon the payment of a specific sum of money to the holder of a trust deed or mortgage, that the lien of the instrument as to a specific described lot or area shall be removed from the blanket lien on the whole area involved.

RELICTION-Gradual recession of water from the usual watermark.

REMAINDER-An interest passing to someone other than the original grantor on the termination of the preceding estate. 

REMITTITUR The certificate of reversal issued by an appellate court upon reversing the judgment appealed from. 

RENTS-A compensation or return yielded periodically by the tenant to the owner in return for the use of property. 

REPLEVIN-A form of action brought for recovery of the possession of personal chattels unlawfully taken from the plaintiff. 

RESCISSION OF CONTRACT-To Annul, to set aside or repeal a contract or agreement.

RESIDUAL-The residue or remainder. 

RESIDUARY LEGATEE-One who receives the residue of an estate after the payment of the testator's debt and legacies. 

RESIDUUM-Balance; residue. 

RESTRICTION-Any limitation in the use of real property. 

REVERSION-The residue of an estate reverting (passing back) to the original grantor or his heirs or assigns at the termination of a preceding estate. In Law, the returning of an estate to the grantor, or his heirs, after a particular estate is ended. 

REVERSIONARY INTEREST-The interest which a person has in the reversion of lands or other property. A right to the future enjoyment of property, at present in the possession or occupation of another.

RIGHT OF SURVIVORSHIP-The right of joint tenants, which, upon the death of one, vests in the survivor sole title to the property. The distinguishing feature of joint tenancy is the right of survivorship. No declaration regarding survivorship is necessary, since it follows as a legal incident.

RIGHT OF WAY-A right to private passage over another's ground. -376-

RIPARIAN RIGHTS—The rights of the owners of lands on the banks of water courses, relating to the water, its use, ownership of soil under the stream, and the accretions thereto. 

SALESMAN-A salesman within the meaning of the Real Estate Act, is one who, for a compensation, is employed by a licensed real estate broker to sell, or offer for sale, or to list, or to buy, or to offer to buy, or to negotiate the purchase or sale or exchange of real estate, or to solicit for prospective purchasers of real estate, or to negotiate a loan on real estate, or to lease, or to negotiate the sale, purchase or exchange of leases, or offer to lease, rent or place for rent, any real estate, or improvements thereon.

SANDWICH LEASE-Any leasehold interest lying between the fee ownership and the final active sublease, is known as a sandwich lease. It is considered less desirable than the underlying fee, as an income producing property and may be considered equivalent to a second mortgage, while the fee would be equivalent to the first mortgage. A sandwich lease provides an annual income without possibility of increment, and has the obligation of the lease as a liability. Therefore, the usual rate of capitalization of a sandwich lease is from 7 to 10 per cent, or even 12 per cent, depending upon the security, obligations and other conditions of the subsequent sublease. SANS-Without.

SATISFACTION-Settlement of a claim or demand; discharge of an obligation, as satisfaction of mortgage. 

SCILICET-To wit; that is to say. Abbreviated as ss (used in acknowledgments).

SEAL-Any impression, device, sign or mark which gives by statute law, the power to authenticate. 

SECTION (Of Land)—A division or parcel of land, comprising one square mile, or 640 acres. Each "Township" (six miles square) is divided by straight lines into 36 sections. 

SECURITY-Protection; assurance; indemnification. The term is usually applied to an obligation, pledge, mortgage, deposit, lien, etc., given by a debtor in order to secure the payment or performance of his debt.

SEIZIN) The possession of land under a claim of a freehold. 

SEISIN)—That which is possessed. The act of taking possession.

SEPARATE PROPERTY—That property acquired by husband or wife as their separate property; i. e., by will, deed or gift so specified, or by their earnings from such property covered by such will, deed, or gift, or that property owned by husband or wife prior to their marriage; that conveyed by either husband or wife to the other as the latter's separate property; the earnings or savings of the wife, and/or of her minor children living with her, or in her custody, while she is living separate from her husband. -377-

SERIATIM-In succession. 

SET-BACK ORDINANCE—An Ordinance making it unlawful to erect any structure between the space specified as a building line and the street. (This does not apply, however, to cornices, canopies, eaves, fire escapes, porches, etc., extending within the restricted space.)

SEVERALTY OWNERSHIP-Held by a person in his own right only, without any other person being joined or connected with him, in point of interest during his estate therein. 

SIGNATURE-The name of a person as written in his own hand, signifying that the writing preceding it accords with his own wishes or intention (the "Signature" to a deed may be made either by the grantor affixing his own signature, or by adopting one written for him, or by making his mark, or impressing some other sign or symbol on the paper by which the signature though written by another for him, may be identified). In some cases, a printed, typewritten, or rubber-stamped name may constitute a valid signature.

SIGNS The Real Estate Act as amended in 1937, "Ch. 757” provides that each individual, firm or corporation licensed as a broker under the provisions of this act shall erect and maintain a sign in a conspicuous place on the premises to indicate that he or it is a licensed real estate broker and the name of said individual, firm or corporation shall be clearly shown thereon. The size and place of such sign shall conform to regulations that may be adopted by the Real Estate Commissioner. 

SINGLE v. UNMARRIED-A single person is one who has never been married. An unmarried person is one who has been divorced and never remarried.

SITUS Location. 

SPECIAL ASSESSMENTS-Those assessments provided by Statute or Ordinance under which property owners are assessed (or taxed) for Municipal improvements in the vicinity of, and presumably improving, their property, such as street improvements, street lighting, etc. 

SS-Namely, to wit.

STARE DECISIS-The doctrine that the decisions of court should stand as precedents for future guidance. (Let that which has been decided stand.)

STATEMENT OF IDENTITY-In effect, an abstract of an individual. A statement required by Title Companies from an individual by which their identity may be authenticated. 

STATUTE LAW-Those laws enacted by the Legislature in contrast to, and extending beyond unwritten or common law. 

STATUTES—Acts of the Legislature; the written will of the Legislature, solemnly expressed according to the forms necessary to constitute it the Law of the State. -378-

STRAIGHT LINE DEPRECIATION-A fixed annual charge against the value of property to offset depreciation and obsolescence. 

SUBDIVISIONS-Land or lands divided or proposed to be divided for the purpose of sale or lease, whether immediate or future, into five or more lots or parcels. 

SUBJECT TO MORTGAGE-When a grantee takes a title to real property subject to mortgage, he is not responsible to the holder of the promissory note for the payment of any portion of the amount due. The most that he can lose in the event of a foreclosure is his equity in the property. See also "Assumption of

Mortgage" in this section. In neither case is the original maker of the note released from his responsibility. 

SUBORDINATE To make subject. 

SUBORDINATION CLAUSE-A clause providing that a certain mortgage or trust deed (the second or third) shall remain subordinate to a specified existing mortgage or trust deed (the first or second lien) or any renewal or extension of the same. 

SUBPOENA-A legal writ summoning a person to appear in Court. 

SUBROGATION-Putting one thing in place of another; substituting one creditor for another.

SURETY-A person who binds himself to pay a sum of money or perform some act in case of the failure of another to do so. A guarantor for another person.

TAX-DEED-The conveyance given upon the sale of land made for non-payment of taxes; the deed whereby the officer of the law undertakes to convey the title of the proprietor to the purchaser at the tax sale.

TAXES The enforced proportional contribution of persons and property levied by the authority of the state, municipality or county, for the support of the government, and for all public needs; any contribution imposed by government upon individuals, for the use and service of the State, whether under the name of toll, tribute, duty, custom, excise, subsidy, aid, assessment, or other name.

TENANCY IN COMMON-Generally defined as two or more persons who hold the same land together by several and distinct titles, or by unity of possession, because none knows his own severalty, and therefore they all occupy promiscuously; where two or more hold the same land with interest accruing under different titles, or accruing under the same title, or conferred by words or limitation, importing that the grantees are to take in distinct shares. In effect, a partnership. 

TENANT-One who holds lands of another; one who has the temporary use and occupation of real property owned by another person (called the "Landlord,") the duration and terms of his tenancy being usually fixed by an instrument called a "lease." 

In the broader legal sense, the word "Tenant" is much more comprehensive than in the common or restricted use of the word. A tenant, speaking in the broadest legal sense is one -379-

who holds land or tenements by any kind of right or title, whether it be in fee, for life, for years, at will, or otherwise. 

TENURE IN LAND-The mode or manner by which a man holds an estate in lands. 

TESTAMENT-An instrument providing for the disposal of property to take place after the owner's decease, according to his desire and direction.

Strictly speaking, the term denotes only a will of personal property; a will of land not being called a "testament," hence, the heading of a formal will usually begins: "This is the last will and testament of me, A. B.," etc.

TESTATE-One who has made a will; one who dies leaving a will. 

TESTATOR-One who makes or has made a testament or will; one who dies leaving a will.

TESTIMONIUM CLAUSE-The concluding clause of an instru ment, beginning "In witness whereof.

" 

TIME IS THE ESSENCE—A term used in contracts where the par ties evidently contemplated a punctual performance, at the precise time named, as vital to the agreement, and one of its essential elements.

TITLE-The means whereby the owner of land has the just possession of his property; the means whereby the person's right to property is established; the instrument which is evidence of such right.

TITLE INSURANCE-Insurance against loss or damage resulting from defects or failure of title to a particular parcel of realty, or from the enforcement of liens existing against it at the time of the insurance.

A "certificate of title" merely expresses formally the professional opinion of the company's examiner that the title is complete and perfect (or otherwise, as stated), and the company is liable only for a want of care, skill, or diligence on the part of its examiner; whereas an "insurance of title" warrants the validity of the title in any and all events. It is not always easy to distinguish between such insurance and a "guarantee of title," except that in the former case the maximum limit of liability is fixed by the policy, while in the latter case the undertaking is to make good any and all loss resulting from defect or failure of the title.

TOPOGRAPHY-The description of a particular place, as a city, town, manor, parish, or a tract of land, especially the exact and scientific delineation and description in minute detail of any place or region.

TORRENS TITLE-A simplified method of transferring title to real property. 

TORT-Wrong; injury; the opposite of right; a legal wrong committed upon the person or property independent of contract. -380-

TOWNSHIP-In the surveys of the public land of the United States, a "township" is a division of territory six miles square, containing 36 sections.

TRUST DEED-An instrument used for the conveyance of land to trustees to secure the payment of debt, with the power of sale upon default, and upon a trust to apply the net proceeds to paying the debt and to turn over the surplus to the grantor. 

TRUSTEE-A person holding property in trust.

TRUSTOR-A Trustor as used in real estate practice in California, is the grantor in a deed of trust; the borrower.

ULTRA VIRES-Beyond their powers. A corporation is said to act "ultra vires" when it exceeds the authority imparted to it. 

UNDUE INFLUENCE-More than necessary; not proper; illegal; persuasion carried to the point of overpowering the will, or such a control over a person as prevents him from acting intelligently, understandingly, and voluntarily, and in effect destroys his free agency, and constrains him to do what he would not have done if such control had not been exercised. 

USURY-Unlawful interest; a premium or compensation paid or stipulated to be paid for the use of money borrowed or returned, beyond the rate of interest established by law. 

In California, the legal rate of interest is 7%, but a rate not to exceed 10% may be agreed upon by contract. Interest above 

10% is usury.

VALUATION-The act of ascertaining the worth of a thing. The estimated worth of a thing.

VENDEE-Purchaser. 

VENDOR-Seller.

VENUE-The neighborhood, place or county in which an injury is declared to have been done, or fact declared to have happened; the county in which an action or prosecution is brought for trial. 

VERIFICATION-Confirmation of the correctness, truth, or authenticity of an instrument, by an affidavit, oath, or deposition. 

VERSUS-Against. (Abbreviated vs. or v.). 

VIDE-See. 

VIDELICET-To-wit; that is to say. 

VIZ.-Videlicet; namely.

VOID-Null; ineffectual; having no legal force or binding effect. 

VOIDABLE That may be avoided, or declared void; not absolutely void, or void in itself. 

WAIVER-To relinquish; to throw away.

WARRANTY-A guarantee that goods or title are as represented. 

WATER TABLE-The depth below the surface of the ground at which water will be found.

ZONE The area set off by the proper authorities for specific use; subject to certain restrictions or restraints. -381-
